You are Archon Horizon's Horizon agent. You turn the blueprints into checked Lean: you pick the most valuable next piece of formalization and carry it as far as you can in one session. You receive the same workspace context Ground saw — roadmap, inbox, memory, blueprint summary, and any Ground orientation — but you choose the strategy from the live Lean state.

You have broad freedom at the workspace level. You may change the route, fill infrastructure gaps, refactor proof APIs, edit blueprint material, update roadmap comments, retrieve references, delegate to subagents, and write local helper scripts/tools when that helps, make substantial changes in the global strategy. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance, you should not defer and postpone hard nodes, you should commit to them and build the infrastructure needed to make progress.

Make concrete progress on the ASSIGNED task's real objective — do not preemptively stop or pivot to easy unrelated wins because the objective is large. A node being big, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib infrastructure is NOT a reason to skip it: start it, build the missing lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as you genuinely can.

Operational norms:
- Use the Lean LSP MCP for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest faithful Lean/lake check.
- Use skills as needed for Lean checks, inbox coordination, commits, references, and subagents.
- Use `"$HORIZON_BIN"` for Horizon CLI actions; write inbox/task/roadmap comments with `--author horizon`.
- Commit coherent progress yourself with `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<math-first message>" <files>`.
- Record durable dead ends as memory and explain important route changes in your final report.
- Use your own tools as you want.

# Skills
Invoke the Horizon CLI via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var (an absolute path), e.g. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --json` — a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.
Most `horizon` commands accept `--json`; use it for AI-friendly output when reading state or ids.
Capability know-how lives in skill files under the workspace `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Claude Code surfaces them automatically; on other engines read the files directly). Consult the relevant one before acting (exact inbox verbs, lean checks, blueprint conventions, the dependency DAG):
- blueprint-conventions — The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
- horizon-commit — Record your own work in the workspace ledger with semantic commits via `horizon commit` — small, meaningful, math-first messages; safe under concurrent runs.
- horizon-inbox — Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter agent-ready items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create, and message other projects via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
- horizon-waiting — How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
- lean-check — Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
- leandag — Consult and refresh the blueprint dependency DAG (leandag) — declaration dependencies, cones, proved status, isolated/dangling nodes, verified union/intersection across projects — via `horizon leandag` and the cached DAG files.
- leansearch — Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
- mathlib-conventions — Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
- project-git — How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
- references — The shared workspace-root references/ library and its manifest.yaml — how to find, read, and cite original sources with \source{...}. Read the source before you cite it (never speculate); anchor TeX sources by slug, and for PDF-only sources extract the LaTeX first (vision, never OCR).
- subagents — How the Ground agent delegates to native subagents to divide review/upkeep work — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, model tiers, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
- task-status — What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, keep each node faithfully aligned with the Lean it names, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

# Memory
- Milne 3.1/3.2 extension chain: "CodimOneFree ⇒ extension to a complete target" is FALSE — never re-add it; the honest chain and the reusable Mathlib extension recipe.

- **Do not reintroduce** an `extend_of_codimOneFree_of_smooth`-style statement (codim-1-free rational map to a complete variety extends): counterexample $\mathbb P^2 \dashrightarrow \mathbb P^1$ away from a point (indeterminacy = one codim-2 point, no regular extension; blow-up needed). - **Honest chain** (all in `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean` + `Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`): Milne 3.1 = `indeterminacy_codimGe2_of_smooth_of_complete` (proved, valuative); Milne 3.3 (`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme`, the only remaining sorry) must assert the codim-1 witness lies **in $Z(f)$** (without that conjunct the disjunct is nearly vacuous and cannot force emptiness); 3.3 + 3.1 ⇒ $Z(f)=\emptyset$ (`av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`); then extension. **Stacks 0AVF / Auslander–Buchsbaum depth-≥2 is NOT needed anywhere in this chain** (supersedes older notes listing 0AVF as a Milne-3.1 blocker).
- **Recipe: extension from empty indeterminacy** (`existsUnique_hom_of_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`, reduced X / separated Y): witness `X.topIso.inv ≫ X.homOfLE hdom.ge ≫ f.toPartialMap.hom` where `hdom : f.toPartialMap.domain = ⊤` (`toPartialMap.domain = f.domain` is `rfl`); rational-class equality via `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mpr ⟨⊤, …⟩` + `simp only [PartialMap.restrict_hom, Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap, Scheme.topIso_hom, Scheme.ι_toIso_inv_assoc, Scheme.homOfLE_homOfLE_assoc]`; uniqueness via `hom_ext_of_toRationalMap_eq` (= `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mp` + `Opens.isDominant_ι` + `ext_of_isDominant`, positional arg — the parser rejects `(ι := …)` named form here). Both lemmas need `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false` BEFORE the docstring (`(restrict …).domain` / `Hom.toPartialMap` defeq walls).
- **Standing lesson**: before attacking a long-lived typed `sorry`, sanity-check the statement for truth (hunt small counterexamples); a false pinned statement silently blocks a whole cone and can smuggle wrong `\uses` (here it dragged a phantom `cor:regular_cohen_macaulay`/0AVF dependency into the blueprint for ~30 iterations).

State after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements — Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):

- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.
- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` — no defeq walls anywhere in this file).
- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) — `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.

**Caveat 1 — pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/étale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now — record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.

**Caveat 2 — `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free ℤ/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, étale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient ⟨sorry⟩` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only. Do NOT reintroduce a global instance, and do NOT try to prove the theorem as stated.
- **`pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` (FBC leaf, `CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:186`) is NOT a cheap adjointness win — Ground's recommendation had the variance backwards. Route analysis (session 0013), do not re-derive.**

- The recommendation claimed "flat `g^*` is a left adjoint, so left-exactness follows from adjointness" — **false**: left adjoints preserve COLIMITS. Left-exactness of flat pullback is genuine flatness content, checked on stalks.
- No dodge exists at the presheaf level: `PresheafOfModules.pullback` is a bare `leftAdjoint` with no pointwise description; the sections-level formula `colim_{U ⊇ g(U')} M(U) ⊗_{O(U)} O(U')` is only RIGHT-exact (the ring maps are not flat — flatness lives on stalks). Sheafification + `SheafOfModules.forget` both preserve finite limits (Mathlib), so the irreducible core really is stalk-level.
- **Viable honest route** (est. 400–800 LOC of new infra): (1) combinators exist — `Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae` / `preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/ExactFunctor.lean`); (2) Mathlib 2026 has module structure on stalks (`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Stalk.lean`, `PresheafOfModules.germ_smul`) and stalk⊣skyscraper at plain-category level (`Topology/Sheaves/Skyscraper.lean`), plus `mono_iff_stalk_mono`/`isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso` (`Topology/Sheaves/Stalks.lean`); (3) the missing brick is **stalk-of-pullback**: `stalkModule_x ∘ pullback g ≅ extendScalars(stalkMap) ∘ stalkModule_{g x}` — provable by adjoint uniqueness IF a module-level skyscraper right adjoint is built (pushforward of skyscraper = skyscraper at the image); then flat stalk maps (`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`-adjacent, `RingHom.Flat` appLE definition) + `ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat` (`ModuleCat/Descent.lean`) finish via kernel-comparison-on-stalks.
- **Cheaper architectural alternative** if the instance stays stuck: the only consumer is `pullback_mapHC_homologyIso` at line 1545 (`cech_flatBaseChange`, affine S/S'), applied to the Čech complex whose terms are iso to tildes — a complex-specific homology-commutation via `tilde`-exactness (`TildeExactness.lean`) + `pullback_spec_tilde_iso` could replace the general instance, at the cost of a termwise-tilde chain-iso.
- Recipe: building ModuleCat-R morphisms into sheaf-of-modules section objects (v4.31) — the ConcreteCategory.ofHom + presheaf-obj pattern, and the let-fvar IsIso gotcha

Landed in `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen` (`QuotScheme.lean`, T12 run 0010). When you need `f : ModuleCat.of R M ⟶ <sections object>` (e.g. to feed `tilde.map`):

- **Target the honest `ModuleCat R` object** `(modulesSpecToSheaf.obj G).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)` — this is literally the domain module of Mathlib's `fromTildeΓ`/`toOpen`. Do NOT target `moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj G` via `ModuleCat.ofHom`/`→ₗ` type ascriptions: elaboration whnf-unfolds the carrier past `restrictScalars`, and `Module R <unfolded carrier>` synthesis then fails (no refold; a letI at the folded form does not match either).
- **Construct via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom { toFun := ..., map_add' := ..., map_smul' := ... }`** with the expected hom type ascribed — the instances come from the objects via the `(· →ₗ[R] ·)` FC family, no synthesis. A bare `let blin : M →ₗ[R] <object> := ...` fails; skipping the standalone LinearMap and going straight to the categorical hom works.
- **map_smul' across compHom-vs-restrictScalars actions**: `change` the goal to the native-action form `(ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom r • f x`, then `rw [← hact]; exact h1` where `hact : appLE V ⊤ e = (ΓSpecIso R).inv` (proved by `rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE, fromSpec_app_self, Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, Subsingleton.elim _ (𝟙 ⊤), op_id, map_id, comp_id]`).
- **IsIso of `tilde.map b'` for a `let`-bound b'**: `haveI : IsIso (tilde.map b') := by rw [show tilde.map b' = (tilde.functor _).map b' from rfl]; infer_instance` FAILS (zeta-expansion mismatch between goal and local instance). Use `inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((tilde.functor _).map b'))` — works even without `clear_value`.
- **Unit-component bijectivity at open immersions**: `Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction j) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j) N` + `restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app` (plain presheaf restriction along `j''ᵁj⁻¹ᵁV = V`) + component of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`. When `rw [← AddCommGrpCat.comp_apply]` fails with "target not type-correct under instances transparency" (`Γ((𝟭 X.Modules).obj N, V)` forms), do `change`-restatement at the type-correct form, then close with `exact congrArg (fun φ => (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom φ) y) hcomp` where `hcomp : f ≫ g = 𝟙 _` — both sides defeq, no rewriting in the wall.
- **Σ-pair trace**: `tilde.toOpen_map_app` (naturality) + `toOpen_fromTildeΓ_app` at `⊤` (+ `homOfLE le_top = 𝟙 ⊤` by `Subsingleton.elim`) give `(tilde.map b' ≫ fromTildeΓ).app ⊤ ∘ toOpen = b'` elementwise, via `congrArg`-chains only.

### 4.4 Why one plus suffices: the separatedness ledger

**(C1) Separatedness** (`Picard/Separatedness.lean`): for affine `T` and a presented étale
cover `E`, the map `relPic C T → relPic C (T' E)` is injective. This is Kleiman 2.5(1)
restricted to what we consume, recast on cocycles. Proof ledger (all pieces named because they
are shared bricks):

1. `sectionsBaseChange` (`Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean`): for `V ⊆ C.left` affine open
   and a `k`-algebra `A`, `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, V_A) ≅ Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A`, naturally.
   *Shared with*: the T₀ dual-numbers engine (`A = k[ε]`, recon lesson 7) and the χ-ledger over
   field extensions (`A = K`). One brick, three consumers.
2. `universalSections` (`Picard/UniversalSections.lean`): `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, ⊤) = A` for
   every `k`-algebra `A` — the two-cover H⁰ slice: the complex
   `Γ(V₀) ⊕ Γ(V₁) → Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` has `H⁰ = k` (Wave 1), stays exact under the flat `⊗[k] A`
   by 1. This is our discharge of Kleiman's `ex:gc&r` hypothesis in the form actually consumed.
3. `prPullback_injective`: `CechPic.map (snd C T).left` is injective for affine `T` — a unit
   cocycle on `C ⊗ T` trivializing must have come from `T`, because
   `𝒪ˣ((C ⊗ V).left) = Γ(V)ˣ` by 2 (applied on an affine pointed cover of `T`). Hence the
   H_T-quotient loses nothing it shouldn't, and "which `N`" in a `pr^*N`-equation is unique.
4. `Descent/InvertibleModule.lean` (pure algebra, PR-candidate): along a faithfully flat ring
   map `A → B`, an invertible `B`-module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
   `A`-module, uniquely up to canonical isomorphism. (Survey: this exists **nowhere** in
   mathlib — "no effective descent of modules"; it is the honest algebraic core of both (C1)
   and (C2).)
5. Assembly (Kleiman's 2.5(1) argument recast): a class `λ ∈ relPic C T` dying on the cover
   gives, via 3 applied over `T'` and `T' ×_T T'`, a line-bundle class `n'` on `T'` with a
   descent datum along `Spec B → Spec A`; by 4 it descends to `n` on `T`, and `λ = pr^* n`
   follows from 3 again. Hence `λ = 0` in the quotient.

**Ledger status (run 0027, session 0014).** Bricks 1–4 are LANDED axiom-clean: 1 =
`Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean`; 2 = `Picard/UniversalSections.lean`; 3 =
`Picard/Separatedness.lean` (`Over.prPullback_injective`, proved for **arbitrary** `T`, not
just affine `T` — see below) on top of `Picard/RefinementInjectivity.lean`; 4 =
`Descent/ModuleDescent.lean` + `Descent/InvertibleModule.lean`. Blueprint:
`sec:PicardEtale` "Separatedness I" section (12 nodes, all `\leanok`).

Two structural discoveries from landing brick 3, binding for item 5:

- **The anticipated "restriction bridge" `(C⊗T)|_{pr⁻¹V} ≅ C ⊗ Spec Γ(V)` is NOT needed and
  was not built.** Instead the qcqs `pushoutSection` square of mathlib
  (`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`) is applied directly to the
  pullback square `(C ⊗ T).left = C ×_k T.left` with the *affine slot on the `T` side*
  (`U_T := V` affine open of `T.left`, `U_X := ⊤ ⊆ C.left` qcqs), giving
  `Γ(T.left, V) ≅ Γ((C⊗T).left, pr⁻¹V)` (`Over.isIso_appLE_snd`) for arbitrary `T` — flatness
  of `T.hom` is free over a field (`Flat.of_field`). Injectivity then extends to arbitrary
  opens `W` by sheaf separation over the affine basis (`Over.appLE_snd_injective`), which is
  why brick 3 needs **no** affineness/quasi-separatedness hypothesis on `T`.
- **The "fiberwise cocycle-glue" is exactly degree-1 Čech refinement injectivity**
  (`Scheme.unitsRes_injective`, `Picard/RefinementInjectivity.lean`): a cocycle on `𝒰` whose
  restriction to a refinement is a coboundary is already a coboundary on `𝒰` (glue the
  comparison units `α_z·γ(i,z)⁻¹` by the sheaf axiom). Corollaries
  `CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff` / `CechPic.mk_injective` make every triviality question in the
  refinement colimit decidable on the representing cover — item 5 and the (C2) rigidification
  should both lean on this rather than chasing refinements.

**Item 5 plan (next actionable).** Mathlib (v4.31) HAS the ring-side Picard group:
`CommRing.Pic R` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PicardGroup.lean`) — invertible modules up to
isomorphism, `CommGroup` via tensor, `Pic.mk R M`, `mk_eq_iff : Pic.mk R M = N ↔
Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] N)`, invertible ⇒ finite projective, and the exactness
`1 → Rˣ → Aˣ → (Submodule R A)ˣ → Pic R → Pic A` — so the survey line in item 4 ("exists
nowhere in mathlib") is now half-obsolete: only the *descent* half is ours, the *group of
classes* is mathlib's. The missing dictionary brick is therefore
`cechPicSpecEquiv : (Spec R).CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic R` (file candidate:
`Picard/PicAffine.lean`): (⇐) from an invertible `R`-module `M`, choose local
trivializations on a pointed cover by basic opens trivializing `M` (invertible ⇒ locally
free of rank 1 on a basic-open basis) and take the transition cocycle; class
well-definedness from `CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff`-style calculus. (⇒) from a cocycle on a
pointed cover, the glued submodule of `∏_x Γ(𝒰(x))`-sections (equalizer form, as in
`Descent/ModuleDescent.descended`); invertibility is Zariski-local. Then item 5 reads:
`λ ∈ ker(relPicAlgMap C ι)` lifts to `CechPic` of `C ⊗ Spec A`; its pullback to
`C ⊗ Spec B` is `pr^* n'` with `n' : CechPic (Spec B)` (definition of `relPic` quotient +
brick 3's `mk`-calculus); transporting `n'` through the dictionary, the *two* base changes
of `n'` to `B ⊗_A B` pull back equally along `pr` (both equal the `B⊗B`-restriction of the
lift), hence are equal by brick 3 over `Spec (B ⊗_A B)`; the resulting `Module.DescentDatum`
(coaction extracted from the equality via the dictionary — the coherence for the *comodule*
form needs the cocycle-level data of the lift, not just the class equality; this is the one
genuinely delicate step) descends by brick 4 to `n : CommRing.Pic A`, and `λ = pr^*
(dictionary n)` by brick 3 again, so `λ = 0` in `relPic`. Estimated 2 sessions: one for the
dictionary, one for the assembly.

**Choice discipline (binding).** Constructions like 4's descended module and §2.6(b)'s
uniformizers may use `Classical.choice` *internally*, provided the resulting `CechPic`/`relPic`
**class** is proven independent of the choices (the allowed axiom set is `propext,
Classical.choice, Quot.sound`). What remains forbidden (route rule 3/4) is storing mere
existence (`Nonempty`) where downstream needs data — in particular the `JacobianData` fields.

**(C2) Comparison under a section** (`Picard/Rigidification.lean`; statement Wave 3, proof may
slip to Wave 4 — OPEN-2): if `C ⊗ T → T` has a section `σ` (equivalently `T ⟶ C ⊗ T` over
`T`), then `picEtAffUnit : relPic C T → PicEtAff C T` is bijective. This is Kleiman 2.5(2)
recast; ledger: `lm:idn` (rigidified pairs = relPic, cocycle form: normalize a cocycle so that
`σ`-pullback is 1), `lm:aut` (no automorphisms: a unit on `C ⊗ T` restricting to 1 along σ is
1, by `universalSections`), then effectivity of the rigidified descent datum by Zariski-locally
reducing to brick 4 on an affine pointed cover of `C ⊗ T` (the datum's cocycle coherence comes
free from the equalizer + rigidification, per Kleiman's triple-product argument, read). Wave 4
consumes (C2) **only** over `k'`-bases where `C(k') ≠ ∅` supplies the section.

8	/-!
9	# The definitional Picard group: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf
10	
11	For a scheme `X`, this file defines the Picard group of record of this development:
12	the Čech cohomology `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site, computed on **pointed
13	covers** (one open per point of `X`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle`) and
14	stabilized along the refinement preorder.
15	
16	## Main declarations
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic`: the Picard group `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` as the quotient
19	  of `Σ 𝒰, X.unitsH1 𝒰` by agreement on a common refinement, with its `CommGroup`
20	  structure and the constructor/eliminator API `CechPic.mk`, `CechPic.ind`,
21	  `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff`, `CechPic.mk_unitsRes`, `CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map`: contravariant functoriality — for
23	  `f : X ⟶ Y` the pullback `Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic` — with the strict functor laws
24	  `CechPic.map_id` and `CechPic.map_comp` (the lane keystone).
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`: on a scheme with a
26	  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.
27	-/
28	
29	set_option autoImplicit false
30	
31	universe u
32	
33	open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
34	
35	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
36	
37	namespace Scheme
38	
39	variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
40	
41	/-! ## The Picard group  -/
42	
43	instance cechPicSetoid (X : Scheme.{u}) : Setoid (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) where
44	  r p q := ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1),
45	    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2
46	  iseqv := by
47	    constructor
48	    · exact fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, le_rfl, le_rfl, rfl⟩
49	    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
50	      exact ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, e.symm⟩
51	    · rintro p q r ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩
52	      refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_left.trans h₁, inf_le_right.trans h₄, ?_⟩
53	      have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
54	      have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
55	      simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
56	      exact e₁'.trans e₂'
57	
58	/-- The definitional Picard group of a scheme: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf,
59	stabilized along refinement of pointed covers. -/
60	def CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
61	  Quotient (cechPicSetoid X)
62	
63	namespace CechPic
64	
65	/-- The Picard class of a unit Čech `H¹` class on a pointed cover. -/
66	def mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : X.CechPic :=
67	  ⟦⟨𝒰, a⟩⟧
68	
69	@[elab_as_elim]
70	theorem ind {motive : X.CechPic → Prop}
71	    (mk : ∀ (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰), motive (mk 𝒰 a)) (x : X.CechPic) :
72	    motive x :=
73	  Quotient.ind (fun p ↦ by obtain ⟨𝒰, a⟩ := p; exact mk 𝒰 a) x
74	
75	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} {a : X.unitsH1 𝒰} {b : X.unitsH1 𝒱} :
76	    mk 𝒰 a = mk 𝒱 b ↔
77	      ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒱),
78	        unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b :=
79	  Quotient.eq
80	
81	/-- Two classes agreeing after restriction to a common refinement are equal; in
82	particular `mk` is invariant under restriction. -/
83	@[simp]
84	theorem mk_unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
85	    mk 𝒱 (unitsRes h a) = mk 𝒰 a :=
86	  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒱, le_rfl, h, unitsRes_rfl _⟩
87	
88	private def mulSig (p q : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
89	    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
90	  ⟨p.1 ⊓ q.1, unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2⟩
91	
92	private lemma mulSig_assoc {𝒰 𝒱 𝒳 : X.PointedCover} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) (b : X.unitsH1 𝒱)
93	    (c : X.unitsH1 𝒳) :
94	    mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳)
95	        (unitsRes inf_le_left (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b) *
96	          unitsRes inf_le_right c)
97	      = mk (𝒰 ⊓ (𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳))
98	        (unitsRes inf_le_left a *
99	          unitsRes inf_le_right (unitsRes inf_le_left b * unitsRes inf_le_right c)) := by
100	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳, le_rfl, (inf_assoc 𝒰 𝒱 𝒳).le, ?_⟩
101	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
102	  exact mul_assoc _ _ _
103	
104	private lemma mulSig_compat {p p' q q' : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰}
105	    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') : mulSig p q ≈ mulSig p' q' := by
106	  obtain ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ := hp
107	  obtain ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩ := hq
108	  have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
109	  have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
110	  simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
111	  refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_inf h₁ h₃, inf_le_inf h₂ h₄, ?_⟩
112	  show unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₁ h₃) (unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2)
113	      = unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₂ h₄) (unitsRes inf_le_left p'.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q'.2)
114	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes]
115	  rw [e₁', e₂']
116	
117	instance : CommGroup X.CechPic where
118	  mul := Quotient.map₂ mulSig (fun _ _ hp _ _ hq ↦ mulSig_compat hp hq)
119	  one := mk ⊤ 1
120	  inv := Quotient.map (fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, p.2⁻¹⟩) (by
121	    rintro p p' ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
122	    exact ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, by simp only [map_inv, e]⟩)
123	  mul_assoc a b c := by
124	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
125	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
126	    induction c using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒳 c =>
127	    exact mulSig_assoc a b c
128	  one_mul a := by
129	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
130	    show mk (⊤ ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left (1 : X.unitsH1 ⊤) * unitsRes inf_le_right a)
131	      = mk 𝒰 a
132	    rw [map_one, one_mul, mk_unitsRes]
133	  mul_one a := by
134	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
135	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ ⊤) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right (1 : X.unitsH1 ⊤))
136	      = mk 𝒰 a
137	    rw [map_one, mul_one, mk_unitsRes]
138	  inv_mul_cancel a := by
139	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
140	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left a⁻¹ * unitsRes inf_le_right a) = mk ⊤ 1
141	    have h : unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) a⁻¹
142	        * unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) a = 1 := by
143	      rw [map_inv]
144	      exact inv_mul_cancel _
145	    rw [h]
146	    exact Quotient.sound ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰, le_rfl, le_top, by rw [map_one, map_one]⟩
147	  mul_comm a b := by
148	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
149	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
150	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b)
151	      = mk (𝒱 ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left b * unitsRes inf_le_right a)
152	    refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱, le_rfl, le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_left, ?_⟩
153	    simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
154	    exact mul_comm _ _
155	
156	lemma one_def : (1 : X.CechPic) = mk ⊤ 1 :=
157	  rfl
158	
159	/-- Multiplication of Picard classes on representatives: restrict both to the common
160	refinement `𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱` and multiply there. Holds by definition. -/
161	lemma mk_mul_mk_inf {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) (b : X.unitsH1 𝒱) :
162	    mk 𝒰 a * mk 𝒱 b
163	      = mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	lemma mk_one (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : mk 𝒰 (1 : X.unitsH1 𝒰) = 1 :=
168	  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒰, le_rfl, le_top, by rw [map_one, map_one]⟩
169	
170	@[simp]
171	lemma mk_mul_mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a b : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
172	    mk 𝒰 a * mk 𝒰 b = mk 𝒰 (a * b) := by
173	  rw [mk_mul_mk_inf]
174	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰, le_rfl, inf_le_left, ?_⟩
175	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_rfl]
176	
177	@[simp]
178	lemma mk_inv (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : (mk 𝒰 a)⁻¹ = mk 𝒰 a⁻¹ :=
179	  rfl
180	
181	/-! ## Functoriality: pullback of Picard classes -/
182	
183	private def mapSig (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : Σ 𝒰 : Y.PointedCover, Y.unitsH1 𝒰) :
184	    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
185	  ⟨p.1.pullback f, f.pullbackUnitsH1 p.1 p.2⟩
186	
187	private lemma mapSig_compat (f : X ⟶ Y) :
188	    ∀ {p q : Σ 𝒰 : Y.PointedCover, Y.unitsH1 𝒰}, p ≈ q → mapSig f p ≈ mapSig f q := by
189	  rintro ⟨𝒰, a⟩ ⟨𝒱, b⟩ ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
190	  refine ⟨𝒲.pullback f, PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₁,
191	    PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₂, ?_⟩
192	  show unitsRes (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₁) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
193	      = unitsRes (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₂) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒱 b)
194	  rw [Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1 f h₁ a, Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1 f h₂ b, e]
195	
196	/-- Contravariant functoriality of the Čech Picard group: pull the cover back pointwise,
197	pull the unit cocycles back through `f`, restrict. -/
198	def map (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic where
199	  toFun := Quotient.map (mapSig f) fun _ _ h ↦ mapSig_compat f h
200	  map_one' := by
201	    show mk ((⊤ : Y.PointedCover).pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 ⊤ 1) = 1
202	    rw [map_one, mk_one]
203	  map_mul' a b := by
204	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
205	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
206	    show mk ((𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).pullback f)
207	        (f.pullbackUnitsH1 (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b))
208	      = mk (𝒰.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) *
209	          mk (𝒱.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒱 b)
210	    rw [mk_mul_mk_inf]
211	    refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).pullback f, le_rfl,
212	      le_inf (PointedCover.pullback_mono f inf_le_left)
213	        (PointedCover.pullback_mono f inf_le_right), ?_⟩
214	    simp only [map_mul, ← Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
215	
216	@[simp]
217	lemma map_mk (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) (a : Y.unitsH1 𝒰) :
218	    map f (mk 𝒰 a) = mk (𝒰.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) :=
219	  rfl
220	
221	/-- Pullback of Picard classes along the identity is the identity. -/
222	@[simp]
223	theorem map_id (X : Scheme.{u}) : map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id X.CechPic := by
224	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_
225	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
226	  show mk (𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X)) ((𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) = mk 𝒰 a
227	  have hle : 𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X) ≤ 𝒰 := fun x ↦ le_of_eq (by simp)
228	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X), le_rfl, hle, ?_⟩
229	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
230	  refine congrArg (Quot.mk _) ?_
231	  ext x y T a b
232	  rw [OneCocycle.res_ev, OneCocycle.res_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev,
233	    γ.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf]
234	  exact id_unitsAppLE _ _
235	
236	/-- Pullback of Picard classes along a composite (the lane keystone). -/
237	theorem map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : map (f ≫ g) = (map f).comp (map g) := by
238	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_
239	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
240	  show mk (𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g)) ((f ≫ g).pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
241	    = mk ((𝒰.pullback g).pullback f)
242	        (f.pullbackUnitsH1 (𝒰.pullback g) (g.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a))
243	  have hle : 𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g) ≤ (𝒰.pullback g).pullback f := fun x ↦ le_of_eq (by simp)
244	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g), le_rfl, hle, ?_⟩
245	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
246	  refine congrArg (Quot.mk _) ?_
247	  ext x y T a b
248	  rw [OneCocycle.res_ev, OneCocycle.res_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev,
249	    Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf, unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE]
250	  rfl
251	
252	/-! ## Sanity gate: triviality over a field -/
253	
254	/-- On a scheme with a subsingleton underlying space — e.g. `Spec` of a field — the
255	Čech Picard group is trivial: every pointed cover is a cover by a single open, on which
256	every unit cocycle is a coboundary. -/
257	instance subsingleton_of_subsingleton (X : Scheme.{u}) [Subsingleton X] :
258	    Subsingleton X.CechPic := by
259	  refine ⟨fun p q ↦ ?_⟩
260	  induction p using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
261	  induction q using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
262	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱, inf_le_left, inf_le_right, ?_⟩
263	  have := H1.subsingleton_of_forall_le (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
264	    (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens (fun i j ↦ le_of_eq (congrArg _ (Subsingleton.elim i j)))
265	  exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
266	
267	/-- The Čech Picard group of the spectrum of a field is trivial. -/
268	theorem eq_one_of_subsingleton (X : Scheme.{u}) [Subsingleton X] (x : X.CechPic) :
269	    x = 1 :=
270	  Subsingleton.elim x 1
271	
272	example {K : Type u} [Field K] (x : (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).CechPic) : x = 1 :=
273	  eq_one_of_subsingleton _ x
274	
275	end CechPic

9	/-!
10	# Unit-valued Čech cocycles on pointed covers and their pullback
11	
12	This file sets up the cocycle-level substrate of the Čech Picard group
13	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic`):
14	
15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PointedCover`: one open per point, containing it; a
16	  `SemilatticeInf` with an `OrderTop`, refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`,
17	  and pullback along a morphism of schemes.
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsCocycle`, `Scheme.unitsH1`: unit-valued Čech 1-cocycles
19	  and `H¹` on a pointed cover; `Scheme.unitsRes`: restriction along a refinement, a group
20	  homomorphism, strictly functorial (`unitsRes_unitsRes`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsEvInf`, `Scheme.unitsRestrict`: the pair values of a
22	  unit cocycle and restriction of unit sections, retyped through `Γ(X, U)ˣ`. Statements
23	  phrased through these are honestly `Γ`-typed, so `rw`/`simp` work on them; goals arising
24	  from the `OneCochain` field types (whose carriers go through `unitsPresheaf.obj`) are
25	  closed against them by `exact` — the two spellings are definitionally equal.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle`, `Hom.pullbackUnitsH1`: pullback of
27	  unit cocycles and their `H¹` classes along a morphism of schemes, compatible with
28	  restriction (`unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1`) — the substrate for `CechPic.map`.
29	
30	The file starts with generic `evInf` algebra for `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups`
31	(values of cochains/cocycles at binary infima commute with `1`, `*`, `⁻¹`); it lives here
32	only because `CechH1.lean` is at the file-size cap, and should move alongside
33	`OneCochain.evInf` when that file is split for a mathlib PR.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe w' w u

82	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

84	namespace Scheme

86	variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
87	
88	/-! ## Pointed covers -/
89	
90	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. Pointed covers
91	are the index discipline of `Scheme.CechPic`: the index type is the carrier of `X` (so
92	everything stays in `Type u`), refinement is indexwise, and pointwise `⊓` makes the
93	refinement order directed. -/
94	structure PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
95	  /-- The member of the cover attached to a point. -/
96	  opens : X → X.Opens
97	  /-- Each point lies in its member. -/
98	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
99	
100	namespace PointedCover
101	
102	@[ext]
103	lemma ext {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : ∀ x, 𝒰.opens x = 𝒱.opens x) : 𝒰 = 𝒱 := by
104	  cases 𝒰; cases 𝒱
105	  simpa using funext h
106	
107	instance : SemilatticeInf X.PointedCover where
108	  le 𝒱 𝒰 := ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x
109	  le_refl 𝒰 x := le_rfl
110	  le_trans 𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 h₁ h₂ x := (h₁ x).trans (h₂ x)
111	  le_antisymm 𝒰 𝒱 h₁ h₂ := ext fun x ↦ le_antisymm (h₁ x) (h₂ x)
112	  inf 𝒰 𝒱 :=
113	    { opens := fun x ↦ 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x
114	      mem_opens := fun x ↦ ⟨𝒰.mem_opens x, 𝒱.mem_opens x⟩ }
115	  inf_le_left 𝒰 𝒱 x := inf_le_left
116	  inf_le_right 𝒰 𝒱 x := inf_le_right
117	  le_inf 𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 h₁ h₂ x := le_inf (h₁ x) (h₂ x)
118	
119	instance : OrderTop X.PointedCover where
120	  top := { opens := fun _ ↦ ⊤, mem_opens := fun _ ↦ trivial }
121	  le_top _ _ := le_top
122	
123	lemma le_def {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x :=
124	  Iff.rfl
125	
126	@[simp]
127	lemma inf_opens (𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover) (x : X) :
128	    (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x = 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x :=
129	  rfl
130	
131	@[simp]
132	lemma top_opens (x : X) : (⊤ : X.PointedCover).opens x = ⊤ :=
133	  rfl
134	
135	/-- The pullback of a pointed cover along a morphism of schemes: the pointed cover by
136	preimages, `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`. -/
137	def pullback (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) : X.PointedCover where
138	  opens x := f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f.base x)
139	  mem_opens x := 𝒰.mem_opens (f.base x)
140	
141	@[simp]
142	lemma pullback_opens (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) (x : X) :
143	    (𝒰.pullback f).opens x = f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f.base x) :=
144	  rfl
145	
146	lemma pullback_mono (f : X ⟶ Y) {𝒰 𝒱 : Y.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) :
147	    𝒱.pullback f ≤ 𝒰.pullback f :=
148	  fun x ↦ ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map f.base).map (homOfLE (h (f.base x)))).le
149	
150	end PointedCover
151	
152	/-! ## Unit cocycles on a pointed cover and their restriction -/
153	
154	/-- The unit-valued Čech 1-cocycles of `X` on a pointed cover. -/
155	abbrev unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : Type u :=
156	  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens

163	homomorphism. -/

165	  H1.resHom fun x ↦ homOfLE (h x)

170	    (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : unitsRes h₂ (unitsRes h₁ a) = unitsRes (h₂.trans h₁) a :=

174	lemma unitsRes_rfl {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} {h : 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :

183	/-- The pair value `γ.evInf i j` of a unit Čech cocycle, retyped as a unit section in

187	def unitsEvInf {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j : X) :

193	abbrev unitsRestrict (X : Scheme.{u}) {U W : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U) :
194	    Γ(X, U)ˣ →* Γ(X, W)ˣ :=
195	  Units.map (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom

199	    unitsEvInf (1 : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) i j = 1 :=

204	    unitsEvInf (γ₁ * γ₂) i j = unitsEvInf γ₁ i j * unitsEvInf γ₂ i j :=

208	lemma unitsEvInf_trans {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j k : X) :
209	    X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
210	          𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j)
211	        (unitsEvInf γ i j)
212	      * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right :
213	          𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k ≤ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k)
214	          (unitsEvInf γ j k)

216	          𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens k)
217	          (unitsEvInf γ i k) :=
218	  γ.evInf_trans i j k

221	lemma res_unitsEvInf {𝒲 𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (hle : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰)
222	    (i j : X) :
223	    unitsEvInf (γ.res fun k ↦ homOfLE (hle k)) i j
224	      = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (hle i) (hle j)) (unitsEvInf γ i j) :=

230	/-- Pullback of the cocycle identity: the pair values of a unit cocycle on `Y`, pulled
231	back through `f : X ⟶ Y` to a common open `T`, still satisfy the cocycle identity. -/
232	private lemma pullback_pair_trans (f : X ⟶ Y) {𝒰 : Y.PointedCover}
233	    (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j k : Y) {T : X.Opens}
234	    (e₁ : T ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j)) (e₂ : T ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k))
235	    (e₃ : T ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens k)) :
236	    f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j) T e₁ (unitsEvInf γ i j)
237	      * f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k) T e₂ (unitsEvInf γ j k)
238	      = f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens k) T e₃ (unitsEvInf γ i k) := by
239	  have E : T ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k) :=
240	    fun t ht ↦ ⟨e₁ ht, (e₂ ht).2⟩
241	  have ht := congrArg (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k) T E)
242	    (unitsEvInf_trans γ i j k)
243	  rw [map_mul, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE,
244	    Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE] at ht
245	  exact ht

247	/-- The pullback of a unit 1-cocycle along a morphism of schemes, on the pulled-back
248	pointed cover. -/
249	def pullbackUnitsCocycle (f : X ⟶ Y) (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
250	    X.unitsCocycle (𝒰.pullback f) where
251	  ev x y _ a b :=
252	    f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) _
253	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le) (unitsEvInf γ (f.base x) (f.base y))
254	  ev_precomp x y _ _ φ a b :=
255	    f.unitsAppLE_map (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le) φ.op
256	      (unitsEvInf γ (f.base x) (f.base y))
257	  ev_trans x y z _ a b c :=
258	    pullback_pair_trans f γ (f.base x) (f.base y) (f.base z)
259	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le) (f.le_preimage_inf b.le c.le)
260	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le c.le)

263	lemma pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (x y : X) {T : X.Opens}
264	    (a : T ⟶ (𝒰.pullback f).opens x) (b : T ⟶ (𝒰.pullback f).opens y) :
265	    (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ).ev x y a b
266	      = f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
267	          (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le) (unitsEvInf γ (f.base x) (f.base y)) :=
268	  rfl

273	      = f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y))
274	          ((𝒰.pullback f).opens x ⊓ (𝒰.pullback f).opens y)
275	          (f.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)
276	          (unitsEvInf γ (f.base x) (f.base y)) :=
277	  rfl

281	    f.pullbackUnitsCocycle (1 : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) = 1 := by
282	  ext x y T a b
283	  exact map_one (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
284	    (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le))

288	    f.pullbackUnitsCocycle (γ₁ * γ₂)
289	      = f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ₁ * f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ₂ := by
290	  ext x y T a b
291	  exact map_mul (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
292	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le))
293	    (unitsEvInf γ₁ (f.base x) (f.base y)) (unitsEvInf γ₂ (f.base x) (f.base y))

295	/-- Pullback of unit cocycles commutes with restriction along a refinement. -/
296	lemma pullbackUnitsCocycle_res (h : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
297	    (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ).res (fun x ↦ homOfLE (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h x))
298	      = f.pullbackUnitsCocycle (γ.res (fun y ↦ homOfLE (h y))) := by
299	  ext x y T a b
300	  have h₁ := congrArg
301	    (f.unitsAppLE (𝒲.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒲.opens (f.base y)) T
302	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le))
303	    (res_unitsEvInf h γ (f.base x) (f.base y))
304	  rw [Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE] at h₁
305	  exact h₁.symm

307	/-- Pullback of a single coboundary comparison along a morphism of schemes: the honest
308	`Γ`-typed computation behind `pullbackUnitsCocycle_isCohomologous`. -/
309	private lemma pullback_coboundary (f : X ⟶ Y) {𝒰 : Y.PointedCover}
310	    (γ₁ γ₂ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (α : ∀ i : Y, Γ(Y, 𝒰.opens i)ˣ)
311	    (hα : ∀ i j, Y.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ≤ 𝒰.opens i) (α i)
312	          * unitsEvInf γ₁ i j
313	        = unitsEvInf γ₂ i j
314	          * Y.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right : 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ≤ 𝒰.opens j) (α j))
315	    (x y : X) {T : X.Opens}
316	    (ha : T ≤ (𝒰.pullback f).opens x) (hb : T ≤ (𝒰.pullback f).opens y) :
317	    X.unitsRestrict ha
318	        (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x)) ((𝒰.pullback f).opens x) le_rfl
319	          (α (f.base x)))
320	      * f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
321	          (f.le_preimage_inf ha hb) (unitsEvInf γ₁ (f.base x) (f.base y))
322	      = f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
323	          (f.le_preimage_inf ha hb) (unitsEvInf γ₂ (f.base x) (f.base y))
324	        * X.unitsRestrict hb
325	            (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base y)) ((𝒰.pullback f).opens y) le_rfl
326	              (α (f.base y))) := by
327	  have h' := congrArg
328	    (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T (f.le_preimage_inf ha hb))
329	    (hα (f.base x) (f.base y))
330	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE] at h'
331	  rw [Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map, Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map]
332	  exact h'

334	/-- Pullback of a cohomology relation along a morphism of schemes. -/
335	lemma pullbackUnitsCocycle_isCohomologous {γ₁ γ₂ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰}
336	    (h : γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂) :
337	    (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ₁).IsCohomologous (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ₂) := by
338	  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := h
339	  exact ⟨fun x ↦ f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x)) ((𝒰.pullback f).opens x) le_rfl
340	      (α (f.base x)),
341	    fun x y T a b ↦ pullback_coboundary f γ₁ γ₂ α
342	      (fun i j ↦ hα i j (homOfLE inf_le_left) (homOfLE inf_le_right)) x y a.le b.le⟩
343	
344	/-- The pullback of unit Čech `H¹` classes along a morphism of schemes. -/
345	def pullbackUnitsH1 (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) :
346	    Y.unitsH1 𝒰 →* X.unitsH1 (𝒰.pullback f) where
347	  toFun := Quot.map f.pullbackUnitsCocycle
348	    (fun _ _ h ↦ f.pullbackUnitsCocycle_isCohomologous h)
349	  map_one' := congrArg OneCocycle.class f.pullbackUnitsCocycle_one
350	  map_mul' a b := by
351	    induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ₁ =>
352	    induction b using Quot.ind with | _ γ₂ =>
353	    exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle_mul γ₁ γ₂)

363	      = f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒲 (unitsRes h a) := by
364	  induction a using Quot.ind with
365	  | _ γ => exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle_res h γ)

8	/-!
9	# Refinement injectivity for the unit Čech `H¹`
10	
11	In degree one, Čech cohomology classes on a cover embed into those on any refinement:
12	for pointed covers `𝒲 ≤ 𝒰` of a scheme `X`, the restriction map
13	`unitsRes : X.unitsH1 𝒰 →* X.unitsH1 𝒲` is **injective**
14	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsRes_injective`). Consequently the refinement colimit
15	`Scheme.CechPic` is a colimit of injections: a class `CechPic.mk 𝒰 a` is trivial iff `a`
16	is already trivial on `𝒰` (`CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff`), and `CechPic.mk 𝒰` is injective
17	(`CechPic.mk_injective`) — the classical statement `Ȟ¹(𝒰, 𝒪^*) ↪ Pic(X)`.
18	
19	Mathematically: suppose the restriction to `𝒲` of a unit cocycle `γ` on `𝒰` is the
20	coboundary of a family of units `α z ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒲 z)`. The comparison sections
21	`α z ⋅ γ(i,z)⁻¹ ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z)` agree on overlaps — by the cocycle identity for `γ`
22	and the coboundary relation for `α` — hence glue, the units presheaf being a sheaf, to a
23	unit `β i ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰 i)`; the family `β` exhibits `γ` as a coboundary on `𝒰` itself.
24	
25	This file also provides the sheaf-theoretic substrate as reusable API: gluing
26	(`Scheme.exists_unitsRestrict_eq`) and separation (`Scheme.unitsRestrict_eq_of_locally_eq`)
27	for unit sections, together with the composition law `unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict`.
28	
29	Refinement injectivity is the "fiberwise cocycle glue" of the separatedness ledger
30	(design §4.4) in reusable form; it is consumed by brick 3 (`Over.prPullback_injective`,
31	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Separatedness`) and by the Zariski-sheaf-on-affines corollary
32	of the étale-separatedness theorem (C1).
33	-/
34

47	/-! ## The `unitsRestrict` calculus and the sheaf property for unit sections -/

49	@[simp]
50	lemma coe_unitsRestrict {U W : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U) (u : Γ(X, U)ˣ) :
51	    (X.unitsRestrict h u : Γ(X, W)) = X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op u :=
52	  rfl

54	/-- Restriction of unit sections is transitive. -/
55	@[simp]
56	lemma unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict {U V W : X.Opens} (h₁ : V ≤ U) (h₂ : W ≤ V)
57	    (u : Γ(X, U)ˣ) :
58	    X.unitsRestrict h₂ (X.unitsRestrict h₁ u) = X.unitsRestrict (h₂.trans h₁) u := by
59	  ext
60	  simp only [coe_unitsRestrict]
61	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
62	
63	/-- **Separation for unit sections**: two units on `V` agreeing on all members of a cover
64	of `V` are equal. -/
65	theorem unitsRestrict_eq_of_locally_eq {ι : Type*} {V : X.Opens} {W : ι → X.Opens}
66	    (hle : ∀ i, W i ≤ V) (hcover : V ≤ ⨆ i, W i) (s t : Γ(X, V)ˣ)
67	    (h : ∀ i, X.unitsRestrict (hle i) s = X.unitsRestrict (hle i) t) : s = t := by
68	  ext
69	  exact X.sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq' W V (fun i ↦ homOfLE (hle i)) hcover _ _
70	    (fun i ↦ congrArg Units.val (h i))
71	
72	/-- **Gluing for unit sections**: a family of units on the members of a cover of `V`,
73	compatible on pairwise intersections, glues to a unit on `V`. (The value and the inverse
74	glue separately as sections; the products of the glued sections are locally `1`, hence
75	`1` by separation.) -/
76	theorem exists_unitsRestrict_eq {ι : Type*} {V : X.Opens} {W : ι → X.Opens}
77	    (hle : ∀ i, W i ≤ V) (hcover : V ≤ ⨆ i, W i) (u : ∀ i, Γ(X, W i)ˣ)
78	    (hu : ∀ i j, X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : W i ⊓ W j ≤ W i) (u i)
79	        = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right : W i ⊓ W j ≤ W j) (u j)) :
80	    ∃ s : Γ(X, V)ˣ, ∀ i, X.unitsRestrict (hle i) s = u i := by
81	  have hval : TopCat.Presheaf.IsCompatible X.sheaf.1 W (fun i ↦ ((u i : Γ(X, W i)))) :=
82	    fun i j ↦ congrArg Units.val (hu i j)
83	  have hinv : TopCat.Presheaf.IsCompatible X.sheaf.1 W
84	      (fun i ↦ (((u i)⁻¹ : Γ(X, W i)ˣ) : Γ(X, W i))) := by
85	    intro i j
86	    have h : X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : W i ⊓ W j ≤ W i) (u i)⁻¹
87	        = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right : W i ⊓ W j ≤ W j) (u j)⁻¹ := by
88	      rw [map_inv, map_inv, hu i j]
89	    exact congrArg Units.val h
90	  obtain ⟨sv, hsv, -⟩ :=
91	    X.sheaf.existsUnique_gluing' W V (fun i ↦ homOfLE (hle i)) hcover _ hval
92	  obtain ⟨si, hsi, -⟩ :=
93	    X.sheaf.existsUnique_gluing' W V (fun i ↦ homOfLE (hle i)) hcover _ hinv
94	  have hvi : sv * si = 1 := by
95	    apply X.sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq' W V (fun i ↦ homOfLE (hle i)) hcover
96	    intro i
97	    rw [map_mul, hsv, hsi, map_one]
98	    exact Units.mul_inv _
99	  have hiv : si * sv = 1 := by rw [mul_comm]; exact hvi
100	  exact ⟨⟨sv, si, hvi, hiv⟩, fun i ↦ Units.ext (hsv i)⟩
101	
102	/-! ## Refinement injectivity -/
103	
104	/-- The glued coboundary: if the restriction of the cocycle `γ` on `𝒰` to a refinement
105	`𝒲 ≤ 𝒰` is the coboundary of `α`, then the comparison sections `α z ⋅ γ(i,z)⁻¹` on
106	`𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z` glue to units `β i ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰 i)` exhibiting `γ` as a coboundary on `𝒰`. -/
107	private lemma exists_glued_coboundary {𝒰 𝒲 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰)
108	    (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (α : ∀ z, Γ(X, 𝒲.opens z)ˣ)
109	    (hα : ∀ z z',
110	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens z ⊓ 𝒲.opens z' ≤ 𝒲.opens z) (α z)
111	          * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (h z) (h z')) (unitsEvInf γ z z')
112	        = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (α z')) :
113	    ∃ β : ∀ i, Γ(X, 𝒰.opens i)ˣ, ∀ i j,
114	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ≤ 𝒰.opens i) (β i)
115	          * unitsEvInf γ i j
116	        = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (β j) := by
117	  -- Step 1: for each `i`, glue the comparison sections over the cover
118	  -- `{𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z}_z` of `𝒰 i`.
119	  have key : ∀ i, ∃ βi : Γ(X, 𝒰.opens i)ˣ, ∀ z : X,
120	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z ≤ 𝒰.opens i) βi
121	        = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (α z)
122	          * (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf le_rfl (h z)) (unitsEvInf γ i z))⁻¹ := by
123	    intro i
124	    refine exists_unitsRestrict_eq (fun z ↦ inf_le_left)
125	      (fun w hw ↦ Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨w, hw, 𝒲.mem_opens w⟩) _ (fun z z' ↦ ?_)
126	    -- compatibility on `O := (𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z) ⊓ (𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z')`, from the coboundary relation
127	    -- for `α` and the cocycle identity for `γ` at `(i, z, z')`, both restricted to `O`
128	    have e₁ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
129	      (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) (inf_le_right.trans inf_le_right) :
130	        (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z) ⊓ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z')
131	          ≤ 𝒲.opens z ⊓ 𝒲.opens z')) (hα z z')
132	    have e₂ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
133	      (le_inf (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left)
134	          ((inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right).trans (h z)))
135	          ((inf_le_right.trans inf_le_right).trans (h z')) :
136	        (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z) ⊓ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z')
137	          ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens z ⊓ 𝒰.opens z')) (unitsEvInf_trans γ i z z')
138	    simp only [map_mul, map_inv, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₁ e₂ ⊢
139	    rw [← e₁, ← e₂]
140	    group
141	  choose β hβ using key
142	  -- Step 2: the coboundary relation for `β` holds on the cover `{𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒰 j ⊓ 𝒲 z}_z`
143	  -- of `𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒰 j`, hence everywhere by separation.
144	  refine ⟨β, fun i j ↦ ?_⟩
145	  refine unitsRestrict_eq_of_locally_eq
146	    (W := fun z ↦ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z) (fun z ↦ inf_le_left)
147	    (fun w hw ↦ Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨w, hw, 𝒲.mem_opens w⟩) _ _ (fun z ↦ ?_)
148	  have e₁ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
149	    (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right :
150	      𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z)) (hβ i z)
151	  have e₂ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
152	    (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right :
153	      𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z ≤ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z)) (hβ j z)
154	  have e₃ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
155	    (inf_le_inf le_rfl (h z) :
156	      𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens z))
157	    (unitsEvInf_trans γ i j z)
158	  simp only [map_mul, map_inv, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₁ e₂ e₃ ⊢
159	  rw [e₁, e₂, ← e₃]
160	  group
161	
162	/-- **Refinement injectivity in degree one**: for pointed covers `𝒲 ≤ 𝒰` of a scheme,
163	restriction of unit Čech `H¹` classes along the refinement is injective. -/
164	theorem unitsRes_injective {𝒰 𝒲 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) :
165	    Function.Injective (unitsRes (X := X) h) := by
166	  refine (injective_iff_map_eq_one (unitsRes h)).mpr fun a ha ↦ ?_
167	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
168	  rw [show (1 : X.unitsH1 𝒲) = OneCocycle.class 1 from rfl] at ha
169	  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ :=
170	    (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mp ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ha)
171	  -- restate the coboundary data through the `Γ`-typed interface
172	  have hα' : ∀ z z',
173	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens z ⊓ 𝒲.opens z' ≤ 𝒲.opens z) (α z)
174	          * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (h z) (h z')) (unitsEvInf γ z z')
175	        = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (α z') := by
176	    intro z z'
177	    have h1 := hα z z'
178	    rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul] at h1
179	    rw [← res_unitsEvInf h γ z z']
180	    exact h1
181	  obtain ⟨β, hβ⟩ := exists_glued_coboundary h γ α hα'
182	  rw [show (1 : X.unitsH1 𝒰) = OneCocycle.class 1 from rfl]
183	  refine (OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mpr
184	    ((OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mpr ⟨β, fun i j ↦ ?_⟩)
185	  rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul]
186	  exact hβ i j

188	/-! ## Consequences for the Čech Picard group -/
189	
190	namespace CechPic
191	
192	/-- A Picard class is trivial iff its representing `H¹` class is trivial on its own
193	cover: no refinement is needed. -/
194	@[simp]
195	theorem mk_eq_one_iff {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} {a : X.unitsH1 𝒰} :
196	    CechPic.mk 𝒰 a = 1 ↔ a = 1 := by
197	  constructor
198	  · intro h1
199	    rw [CechPic.one_def] at h1
200	    obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩ := CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff.mp h1
201	    rw [map_one] at e
202	    exact unitsRes_injective h₁ (by rw [e, map_one])
203	  · rintro rfl
204	    exact CechPic.mk_one 𝒰
205	
206	/-- `Ȟ¹(𝒰, 𝒪^*) ↪ Pic(X)`: the Picard class of an `H¹` class on a fixed pointed cover
207	determines it. -/
208	theorem mk_injective (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :
209	    Function.Injective (CechPic.mk 𝒰 : X.unitsH1 𝒰 → X.CechPic) := by
210	  intro a b hab
211	  have h1 : CechPic.mk 𝒰 (a * b⁻¹) = 1 := by
212	    rw [← CechPic.mk_mul_mk, ← CechPic.mk_inv, hab, mul_inv_cancel]
213	  rw [mk_eq_one_iff] at h1
214	  exact mul_inv_eq_one.mp h1
215	
216	end CechPic

16	/-!
17	# The Picard group of a commutative ring
18	
19	This file defines the Picard group `CommRing.Pic R` of a commutative ring `R` as the type of
20	invertible `R`-modules (in the sense that `M` is invertible if there exists another `R`-module
21	`N` such that `M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R`) up to isomorphism, equipped with tensor product as multiplication.
22	
23	## Main definition
24	
25	- `Module.Invertible R M` says that the canonical map `Mᵛ ⊗[R] M → R` is an isomorphism.
26	  To show that `M` is invertible, it suffices to provide an arbitrary `R`-module `N`
27	  and an isomorphism `N ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[R] R`, see `Module.Invertible.right`.
28	
29	- `ClassGroup.equivPic`: the class group of a domain is isomorphic to the Picard group.
30	
31	## Main results
32	
33	- An invertible module is finite and projective (provided as instances).
34	
35	- `Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv`: an invertible module is free iff it is isomorphic to
36	  the ring, i.e. its class is trivial in the Picard group.
37	
38	- `Submodule.ker_unitsToPic`, `Submodule.range_unitsToPic`: exactness of the sequence
39	  `1 → Rˣ → Aˣ → (Submodule R A)ˣ → Pic R → Pic A` at the last two spots.
40	  See Theorem 2.4 in [RobertsSingh1993] or Exercise I.3.7(iv) and Proposition I.3.5 in [Weibel2013].
41	
42	## References
43	
44	- https://qchu.wordpress.com/2014/10/19/the-picard-groups/
45	- https://mathoverflow.net/questions/13768/what-is-the-right-definition-of-the-picard-group-of-a-commutative-ring
46	- https://mathoverflow.net/questions/375725/picard-group-vs-class-group
47	- [Weibel2013], https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.I.pdf
48	- [Stacks: Picard groups of rings](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AFW)
49	
50	## TODO
51	
52	Show:
53	- Invertible modules over a commutative ring have the same cardinality as the ring.
54	
55	- Establish other characterizations of invertible modules, e.g. they are modules that
56	  become free of rank one when localized at every prime ideal.
57	  See [Stacks: Finite projective modules](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NX).
58	- Connect to invertible sheaves on `Spec R`. More generally, connect projective `R`-modules of
59	  constant finite rank to locally free sheaves on `Spec R`.
60	- Exhibit isomorphism with sheaf cohomology `H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`.
61	-/

63	@[expose] public section

65	open TensorProduct

67	universe u v
68	
69	variable (R : Type u) (M : Type v) (N P Q A : Type*) [CommSemiring R]

71	variable [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module R P] [Module R Q]

75	/-- An `R`-module `M` is invertible if the canonical map `Mᵛ ⊗[R] M → R` is an isomorphism,
76	where `Mᵛ` is the `R`-dual of `M`. -/
77	protected class Invertible : Prop where
78	  bijective : Function.Bijective (contractLeft R M)
79	
80	namespace Invertible

82	/-- Promote the canonical map `Mᵛ ⊗[R] M → R` to a linear equivalence for invertible `M`. -/
83	noncomputable def linearEquiv [Module.Invertible R M] : Module.Dual R M ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[R] R :=
84	  .ofBijective _ Invertible.bijective
85	
86	variable {R M N}
87	
88	section LinearEquiv

90	variable (e : M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R)
91	
92	/-- The canonical isomorphism between a module and the result of tensoring it
93	from the left by two mutually dual invertible modules. -/
94	noncomputable abbrev leftCancelEquiv : M ⊗[R] (N ⊗[R] P) ≃ₗ[R] P :=
95	  (TensorProduct.assoc R M N P).symm ≪≫ₗ e.rTensor P ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.lid R P
96	
97	/-- The canonical isomorphism between a module and the result of tensoring it
98	from the right by two mutually dual invertible modules. -/
99	noncomputable abbrev rightCancelEquiv : (P ⊗[R] M) ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] P :=
100	  TensorProduct.assoc R P M N ≪≫ₗ e.lTensor P ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.rid R P
101	
102	variable {P Q} in
103	theorem leftCancelEquiv_comp_lTensor_comp_symm (f : P →ₗ[R] Q) :
104	    leftCancelEquiv Q e ∘ₗ (f.lTensor N).lTensor M ∘ₗ (leftCancelEquiv P e).symm = f := by
105	  rw [← LinearMap.comp_assoc, LinearEquiv.comp_toLinearMap_symm_eq]; ext; simp
106

109	    rightCancelEquiv Q e ∘ₗ (f.rTensor M).rTensor N ∘ₗ (rightCancelEquiv P e).symm = f := by
110	  rw [← LinearMap.comp_assoc, LinearEquiv.comp_toLinearMap_symm_eq]; ext; simp

113	noncomputable def rTensorInv : (P ⊗[R] M →ₗ[R] Q ⊗[R] M) →ₗ[R] (P →ₗ[R] Q) :=
114	  ((rightCancelEquiv Q e).congrRight ≪≫ₗ (rightCancelEquiv P e).congrLeft _ R) ∘ₗ
115	    LinearMap.rTensorHom N

117	theorem rTensorInv_leftInverse : Function.LeftInverse (rTensorInv P Q e) (.rTensorHom M) :=
118	  fun _ ↦ by
119	    simp_rw [rTensorInv, LinearEquiv.coe_trans, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_toLinearMap]
120	    rw [← LinearEquiv.eq_symm_apply]
121	    ext; simp [LinearEquiv.congrLeft, LinearEquiv.congrRight, LinearEquiv.arrowCongrAddEquiv]

124	  simpa [rTensorInv] using (rTensorInv_leftInverse _ _ <| TensorProduct.comm R N M ≪≫ₗ e).injective

129	  __ := LinearMap.rTensorHom M

174	private theorem finite_projective : Module.Finite R M ∧ Projective R M := by
175	  let N := Dual R M
176	  let e : M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R := TensorProduct.comm .. ≪≫ₗ linearEquiv R M
177	  have ⟨S, hS⟩ := TensorProduct.exists_finset (e.symm 1)
178	  let f : (S →₀ N) →ₗ[R] R := Finsupp.lsum R fun i ↦ e.toLinearMap ∘ₗ TensorProduct.mk R M N i.1.1
179	  have : Function.Surjective f := by
180	    rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, Ideal.eq_top_iff_one]
181	    use Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i ↦ i.1.2
182	    simp_rw [f, Finsupp.coe_lsum]
183	    rw [Finsupp.sum_fintype _ _ fun _ ↦ map_zero _]
184	    rwa [e.symm_apply_eq, map_sum, ← Finset.sum_coe_sort, eq_comm] at hS
185	  have ⟨g, hg⟩ := projective_lifting_property f .id this
186	  classical
187	  let aux := finsuppRight R _ M N S ≪≫ₗ Finsupp.mapRange.linearEquiv e
188	  let f' : (S →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M := TensorProduct.rid R M ∘ₗ f.lTensor M ∘ₗ aux.symm
189	  let g' : M →ₗ[R] S →₀ R := aux ∘ₗ g.lTensor M ∘ₗ (TensorProduct.rid R M).symm
190	  have : Function.Surjective f' := by simpa [f'] using LinearMap.lTensor_surjective _ this
191	  refine ⟨.of_surjective f' this, .of_split g' f' <| LinearMap.ext fun m ↦ ?_⟩
192	  simp [f', g', show f (g 1) = 1 from DFunLike.congr_fun hg 1]

194	instance : Module.Finite R M := (finite_projective R M).1
195	instance : Projective R M := (finite_projective R M).2
196	example : IsReflexive R M := inferInstance

198	section inj_surj_bij

203	    Function.Injective (f.lTensor M) ↔ Function.Injective f := by
204	  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _⟩
205	  rw [← leftCancelEquiv_comp_lTensor_comp_symm (linearEquiv R M) f]

208	theorem rTensor_injective_iff {f : N →ₗ[R] P} :
209	    Function.Injective (f.rTensor M) ↔ Function.Injective f := by
210	  rw [← LinearMap.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj, lTensor_injective_iff]

213	    Function.Surjective (f.lTensor M) ↔ Function.Surjective f := by
214	  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, LinearMap.lTensor_surjective _⟩
215	  rw [← leftCancelEquiv_comp_lTensor_comp_symm (linearEquiv R M) f]

220	  rw [← LinearMap.lTensor_surj_iff_rTensor_surj, lTensor_surjective_iff]

223	    Function.Bijective (f.lTensor M) ↔ Function.Bijective f := by

233	variable {R M} in

634	private theorem projective_units_and_mul'_comp_lTensor_bijective (I : (Submodule R A)ˣ) :
635	    Projective R I ∧ Function.Bijective (mul' R A ∘ₗ I.1.subtype.lTensor A) := by
636	  obtain ⟨T, T', hT, hT', one_mem⟩ := mem_span_mul_finite_of_mem_mul (I.inv_mul ▸ one_le.mp le_rfl)
637	  classical
638	  rw [← Set.image2_mul, ← Finset.coe_image₂, mem_span_finset] at one_mem
639	  set S := T.image₂ (· * ·) T'
640	  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := one_mem
641	  choose a ha b hb eq using fun i : S ↦ Finset.mem_image₂.mp i.2
642	  let f : I →ₗ[R] S → R := .pi fun i ↦ (LinearEquiv.ofInjective
643	      (Algebra.linearMap R A) (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective R A)).symm.comp <|
644	    restrict (mulRight R (r i • a i)) fun x hx ↦ by
645	      rw [← one_eq_range, ← I.mul_inv]; exact mul_mem_mul hx (I⁻¹.1.smul_mem _ <| hT <| ha i)
646	  have hf (x : I.1) (i : S) : algebraMap R A (f x i) = x * r i • a i := by
647	    dsimp [f, ← Algebra.linearMap_apply]
648	    exact LinearEquiv.ofInjective_symm_apply ..
649	  let g : (S → R) →ₗ[R] I := .lsum _ _ ℕ fun i ↦ .toSpanSingleton _ _ ⟨b i, hT' <| hb i⟩
650	  have hgf : g ∘ₗ f = .id := LinearMap.ext fun x ↦ Subtype.ext <| by
651	    simp only [g, lsum_apply, comp_apply, sum_apply, toSpanSingleton_apply, proj_apply]
652	    simp_rw [coe_sum, coe_smul, Algebra.smul_def, hf, mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum,
653	      Algebra.smul_mul_assoc, eq, (Finset.sum_coe_sort ..).trans hr.2, mul_one, id_apply]
654	  set m := mul' R A ∘ₗ I.1.subtype.lTensor A
655	  have eq : (piScalarRight R R A S).toLinearMap ∘ₗ f.lTensor A =
656	      (.pi fun i : S ↦ mulRight R (r i • a i)) ∘ₗ m := by
657	    ext; simp [(Algebra.smul_def ..).trans (Algebra.commutes ..), hf, m, mul_assoc]
658	  have := (piScalarRight R R A S).injective.comp <| injective_of_comp_eq_id
659	    (f.lTensor A) (g.lTensor A) <| by rw [← lTensor_comp, hgf, lTensor_id]
660	  rw [← LinearEquiv.coe_toLinearMap, ← coe_comp, eq, coe_comp] at this
661	  refine ⟨.of_split f g hgf, .of_comp this, range_eq_top.mp ?_⟩
662	  rw [show m = mulMap ⊤ I ∘ₗ (topEquiv.symm.rTensor I.1).toLinearMap by ext; rfl, range_comp,
663	    LinearEquiv.range, map_top, mulMap_range, top_mul_eq_top_of_mul_eq_one I.inv_mul]
664

676	/-- Given two invertible `R`-submodules in an `R`-algebra `A`, the `R`-linear map from
677	`I ⊗[R] J` to `I * J` induced by multiplication is an isomorphism. -/
678	noncomputable def tensorEquivMul : I ⊗[R] J ≃ₗ[R] I * J := by
679	  refine .ofBijective _ ⟨.of_comp (f := Submodule.subtype _) ?_, mulMap'_surjective _ _⟩
680	  convert!
681	    (projective_units_and_mul'_comp_lTensor_bijective J).2.1.comp
682	      (Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ I.1.subtype_injective)
683	  simp_rw [← LinearMap.coe_comp]
684	  congr 1; ext; rfl

686	/-- Given an invertible `R`-submodule `I` in an `R`-algebra `A`, the `R`-linear map
687	from `I ⊗[R] I⁻¹` to `R` induced by multiplication is an isomorphism. -/
688	noncomputable def tensorInvEquiv : I ⊗[R] ↑I⁻¹ ≃ₗ[R] R :=
689	  tensorEquivMul I _ ≪≫ₗ .ofEq _ _ (I.mul_inv.trans one_eq_range) ≪≫ₗ
690	    .symm (.ofInjective _ (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective R A))

697	/-- The group homomorphism from the invertible submodules in a faithful algebra over `R` to
698	the Picard group of `R`. See Lemma 2.2 in [RobertsSingh1993]. -/
699	@[simps] noncomputable def unitsToPic : (Submodule R A)ˣ →* Pic R where
700	  toFun I := Pic.mk R I
701	  map_one' := mk_eq_one_iff.mpr
702	    ⟨.ofEq _ _ one_eq_range ≪≫ₗ .symm (.ofInjective _ (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective R A))⟩
703	  map_mul' I J := by rw [← mk_tensor, mk_eq_mk_iff]; exact ⟨(tensorEquivMul I J).symm⟩
704	
705	/-- The image of an invertible `R`-submodule `I ⊆ A` under `unitsToPic` is isomorphic to `I`. -/
706	noncomputable def unitsToPicEquiv (I : (Submodule R A)ˣ) : unitsToPic R A I ≃ₗ[R] I :=
707	  (mk_eq_iff.mp rfl).some.symm

711	theorem ker_unitsToPic :
712	    (unitsToPic R A).ker = (Units.map (spanSingleton R).toMonoidHom).range := by
713	  ext I; constructor <;> intro h
714	  · have e := (mk_eq_one_iff.mp h).some.symm
715	    have e' := (mk_eq_one_iff.mp (inv_mem h)).some.symm
716	    have h := eq_span_singleton_of_surjective e.surjective
717	    have h' := eq_span_singleton_of_surjective e'.surjective
718	    refine ⟨(isUnit_iff_exists_and_exists.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩).unit, Units.ext h.symm⟩
719	    · have : span R {(e 1).1 * e' 1} = 1 := by simpa [span_mul_span] using congr($h * $h').symm
720	      have ⟨r, hr⟩ := span_singleton_eq_one_iff.mp this
721	      exact ⟨e' 1 * algebraMap R A r.inv, by simp [← mul_assoc, hr, ← map_mul]⟩
722	    · have : span R {(e' 1).1 * e 1} = 1 := by simpa [span_mul_span] using congr($h' * $h).symm
723	      have ⟨r, hr⟩ := span_singleton_eq_one_iff.mp this
724	      exact ⟨algebraMap R A r.inv * e' 1, by simp [mul_assoc, hr, ← map_mul]⟩
725	  · obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := h
726	    exact mk_eq_one_iff.mpr ⟨.symm <| (.ofInjective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton R A x) fun _ _ eq ↦
727	      (faithfulSMul_iff_injective_smul_one R A).mp ‹_› <| by simpa using congr($eq * x.inv)) ≪≫ₗ
728	      .ofEq _ _ (by ext; simp [mem_span_singleton])⟩

730	/-- Exactness of the sequence `1 → Rˣ → Aˣ → (Submodule R A)ˣ → Pic R → Pic A`
731	at `(Submodule R A)ˣ`. -/
732	theorem mulExact_unitsMap_spanSingleton_unitsToPic :
733	    Function.MulExact (Units.map (spanSingleton R).toMonoidHom) (unitsToPic R A) :=
734	  MonoidHom.mulExact_iff.mpr (ker_unitsToPic R A)

744	/-- If a flat `R`-module becomes free of rank 1 after base-changing to a faithful `R`-algebra `A`,

773	    convert! (AlgebraTensorModule.congr (.refl ..) (submoduleAlgebraEquiv e) ≪≫ₗ e).bijective
774	    ext x
775	    refine x.induction_on (by simp) ?_ (by simp +contextual)
776	    intro a x
777	    obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := (submoduleAlgebraEquiv e).symm.surjective x
778	    suffices a * toAlgebra e m = e (a ⊗ₜ[R] m) by simpa using! this
779	    dsimp [toAlgebra]
780	    rw [map_one, ← smul_eq_mul, ← map_smul, smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]

815	theorem Submodule.range_unitsToPic : (unitsToPic R A).range = relPic R A := by
816	  ext M; constructor <;> intro h
817	  · obtain ⟨I, rfl⟩ := h
818	    exact mk_eq_one_iff.mpr ⟨AlgebraTensorModule.congr (.refl ..) (unitsToPicEquiv I) ≪≫ₗ
819	      .ofBijective ((Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'' R).toLinearMap ∘ₗ AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor A A
820	        I.1.subtype) (projective_units_and_mul'_comp_lTensor_bijective I).2⟩
821	  have e := (mk_eq_one_iff.mp h).some
822	  have f := (mk_eq_one_iff.mp (inv_mem h)).some
823	  refine ⟨(isUnit_of_mul_isUnit_left (x := submoduleAlgebra e) (y := submoduleAlgebra f) ?_).unit,
824	    mk_eq_iff.mpr ⟨submoduleAlgebraEquiv e⟩⟩
825	  have := eq_span_singleton_of_surjective <| LinearEquiv.surjective <|
826	    (congr (submoduleAlgebraEquiv e) (submoduleAlgebraEquiv f) ≪≫ₗ
827	    (mk_eq_one_iff.mp <| by simp_rw [mk_tensor, mk_eq_self, mul_inv_cancel]).some).symm ≪≫ₗ
828	    tensorSubmoduleAlgebraEquivMul f (submoduleAlgebra e)
829	  rw [this]
830	  apply_fun (⊤ * ·) at this
831	  simp_rw [← mul_assoc, top_mul_submoduleAlgebra] at this
832	  obtain ⟨a, -, eq⟩ := mem_mul_span_singleton.mp (this ▸ mem_top (x := 1))
833	  exact .map (spanSingleton R).toMonoidHom (.of_mul_eq_one_right _ eq)
834	
835	/-- Exactness of the sequence `1 → Rˣ → Aˣ → (Submodule R A)ˣ → Pic R → Pic A` at `Pic R`. -/
836	theorem Submodule.mulExact_unitsToPic_mapAlgebra :
837	    Function.MulExact (unitsToPic R A) (mapAlgebra R A) :=
838	  MonoidHom.mulExact_iff.mpr (range_unitsToPic R A).symm

841	/-- If `A` is a faithful `R`-algebra, the relative Picard group Pic(A/R) is isomorphic to
842	the group of the invertible `R`-submodules in `A` modulo the principal submodules. -/
843	@[simps!] noncomputable def Submodule.unitsQuotEquivRelPic :
844	    (Submodule R A)ˣ ⧸ (Units.map (spanSingleton R).toMonoidHom).range ≃* relPic R A :=
845	  (QuotientGroup.congr _ _ (.refl _) ((Subgroup.map_id _).trans (ker_unitsToPic R A).symm)).trans <|
846	  (quotientKerEquivRange _).trans <| .subgroupCongr (range_unitsToPic R A)
847	
848	/-- The class group of a domain is isomorphic to the Picard group. -/
849	@[simps!] noncomputable def ClassGroup.equivPic (R) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] :
850	    ClassGroup R ≃* Pic R :=
851	  (mulEquivUnitsSubmoduleQuotRange R).trans <| .trans (Submodule.unitsQuotEquivRelPic R _) <|
852	    .trans (.subgroupCongr <| relPic_eq_top R _) Subgroup.topEquiv
853	
854	/-- The Picard group of a domain with normalizable gcd is trivial.
855	This includes unique factorization domains. -/
856	@[stacks 0BCH]
857	instance (R) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [Nonempty (NormalizedGCDMonoid R)] : Subsingleton (Pic R) :=
858	  Equiv.subsingleton (ClassGroup.equivPic R).toEquiv.symm

890	/-- In a total ring of fractions, if two ideals are inverse to each other in the Picard group,
891	the only possibility is that they are both the whole ring. -/
892	theorem Ideal.eq_top_of_mk_tensor_eq_one [IsFractionRing R R] (I J : Ideal R)
893	    [Module.Invertible R I] [Module.Invertible R J] (h : Pic.mk R (I ⊗[R] J) = 1) :
894	    I = ⊤ ∧ J = ⊤ := by
895	  have ⟨e⟩ := mk_eq_one_iff.mp h
896	  have e := e.symm ≪≫ₗ Submodule.LinearDisjoint.mulMap
897	    (.of_left_le_one_of_flat I J <| le_top.trans one_eq_top.ge)
898	  have : IsUnit (e 1 : R) := IsFractionRing.self_iff_nonZeroDivisors_le_isUnit.mp ‹_› <|
899	      IsRegular.mem_nonZeroDivisors <| isRightRegular_iff_isRegular.mp <| by
900	    rw [IsRightRegular]
901	    convert! Subtype.val_injective.comp e.injective using 2
902	    rw [← smul_eq_mul, ← Submodule.coe_smul, ← map_smul, smul_eq_mul, mul_one, Function.comp_apply]
903	  constructor <;> refine eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ ?_ this
904	  exacts [mul_le_right (e 1).2, mul_le_left (e 1).2]
