9	/-!
10	# Faithfully flat descent of modules
11	
12	Let `A → B` be a map of commutative rings and let `M` be a `B`-module.  This file defines
13	descent data on `M` relative to `A → B`, constructs the descended `A`-module `M₀` as an
14	equalizer submodule of `M`, and proves the two fundamental theorems of flat descent for
15	modules:
16	
17	* **effectivity**: if `B` is flat over `A`, the canonical comparison map
18	  `B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` is an isomorphism;
19	* **uniqueness**: if `B` is faithfully flat over `A`, then any `A`-module `N` equipped with
20	  a `B`-module isomorphism `B ⊗[A] N ≃ M` matching the descent datum is canonically
21	  isomorphic to `M₀`.  The engine is the degree `≤ 1` exactness of the Amitsur complex
22	  `0 → N → B ⊗[A] N ⇉ B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] N`.
23	
24	## Design notes
25	
26	* **Comodule form of a descent datum.**  Classically a descent datum on `M` is a
27	  `B ⊗[A] B`-module isomorphism `φ : M ⊗[A] B ≃ B ⊗[A] M` satisfying a cocycle condition
28	  over the triple tensor product.  We use the equivalent *comodule* (Sweedler-coring)
29	  presentation: a `B`-linear coaction `δ : M →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] M` (with `B` acting on the left
30	  tensor factor of the target) such that
31	  - (`counit`) the action map `B ⊗[A] M → M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`, retracts `δ`, and
32	  - (`coassoc`) the two natural liftings of `δ` to `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] M` agree on the image
33	    of `δ`.
34	
35	  The dictionary: given `φ`, set `δ m := φ (m ⊗ₜ 1)`; then `B ⊗ B`-linearity of `φ` makes
36	  `δ` `B`-linear and recovers `φ` via `φ (m ⊗ₜ b) = (1 ⊗ b) • δ m`, the cocycle condition
37	  becomes `coassoc`, and the standard normalization becomes `counit`.  Conversely the `φ`
38	  associated to a coaction is automatically invertible.  This presentation avoids putting
39	  (several!) `B ⊗[A] B`-module structures on `B ⊗[A] M` and `M ⊗[A] B`, which do not exist
40	  as mathlib instances.  For a unit `u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` whose associated `φ` is
41	  `u • ·` on `M = B`, the coaction is `δ x = u.val * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`.
42	
43	* **The descended module** is the equalizer `M₀ = {m : M | δ m = 1 ⊗ₜ m}`, an `A`-submodule
44	  of `M`, realized as the kernel of the `A`-linear map `δ - (1 ⊗ₜ ·)`.
45	
46	* **Effectivity requires only flatness.**  The comparison `B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` is an isomorphism
47	  whenever `B` is flat over `A`: the counit and coassociativity laws make the augmented
48	  complex `M₀ → M ⇉ B ⊗[A] M` contractible after applying `B ⊗[A] -` (the contraction being
49	  the action maps), and flatness identifies `B ⊗[A] M₀` with the corresponding kernel.
50	  Faithful flatness enters only for uniqueness (the Amitsur exactness `N ≅ (B ⊗[A] N)₀`).
51	
52	* Everything is pinned to a single universe `u`; multi-universe binders interact badly with
53	  the tensor-product instance search in downstream files.
54	
55	## Main declarations
56	
57	* `Module.actionMap A B M : B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M`: the action map `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.
58	* `Module.DescentDatum A B M`: descent data on the `B`-module `M` relative to `A → B`,
59	  in comodule form.
60	* `Module.DescentDatum.baseChange A B N`: the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N`.
61	* `Module.DescentDatum.descended`: the descended `A`-submodule `M₀`.
62	* `Module.DescentDatum.comparison`: the canonical map `B ⊗[A] M₀ →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.
63	* `Module.DescentDatum.comparison_bijective`: **effectivity** — `comparison` is bijective
64	  when `B` is a flat `A`-module.
65	* `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv : B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ₗ[B] M`: the comparison isomorphism.
66	* `Module.DescentDatum.exact_mk_coactionSub`: degree `≤ 1` **Amitsur exactness** for a
67	  faithfully flat `A → B`.
68	* `Module.DescentDatum.unitEquiv : N ≃ₗ[A] (baseChange A B N).descended`: the unit of
69	  descent is an isomorphism (faithfully flat case).
70	* `Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended`: **uniqueness** — an `A`-module `N` with a
71	  datum-compatible isomorphism `B ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[B] M` is canonically `A`-isomorphic to `M₀`.
72	  Two descents of the same datum are therefore canonically isomorphic.
73	-/

75	universe u
76	
77	open TensorProduct

79	namespace Module

81	variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
82	variable (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
83	
84	/-- The `B`-linear action map `B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`, of a `B`-module `M`. -/
85	noncomputable def actionMap : B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M :=
86	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (LinearMap.id (R := A) (M := M))
87	
88	@[simp] theorem actionMap_tmul (b : B) (m : M) : actionMap A B M (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • m := rfl
89	
90	theorem actionMap_one_tmul (m : M) : actionMap A B M (1 ⊗ₜ m) = m := by simp
91	
92	variable {A B M}
93	
94	section actionMap
95	
96	variable {X Y : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
97	
98	/-- Naturality of the action map in `B`-linear maps. -/
99	theorem actionMap_baseChange [Module B X] [IsScalarTower A B X]
100	    [AddCommGroup Y] [Module A Y] [Module B Y] [IsScalarTower A B Y]
101	    (g : X →ₗ[B] Y) (x : B ⊗[A] X) :
102	    actionMap A B Y ((g.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x) = g (actionMap A B X x) := by
103	  induction x with
104	  | zero => simp
105	  | tmul b m => simp
106	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
107	
108	/-- The action map of `B ⊗[A] X` retracts the base change of `x ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ x`. -/
109	theorem actionMap_baseChange_mk (x : B ⊗[A] X) :
110	    actionMap A B (B ⊗[A] X) ((TensorProduct.mk A B X 1).baseChange B x) = x := by
111	  induction x with
112	  | zero => simp
113	  | tmul b m => simp [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
114	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
115	
116	end actionMap
117	
118	variable (A B M) in
119	/-- A descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to `A → B`, in comodule (Sweedler-coring)
120	form: a `B`-linear coaction `δ : M → B ⊗[A] M` (`B` acting through the left tensor factor
121	of the target) that is counital and coassociative.  This is equivalent to the classical
122	formulation via a `B ⊗[A] B`-linear cocycle isomorphism `M ⊗[A] B ≃ B ⊗[A] M`; see the
123	module docstring for the dictionary. -/
124	structure DescentDatum where
125	  /-- The coaction of the descent datum. -/
126	  coaction : M →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] M
127	  /-- The action map retracts the coaction. -/
128	  counit (m : M) : actionMap A B M (coaction m) = m
129	  /-- Coassociativity: the two liftings of the coaction to `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] M` agree on
130	  coaction values.  In the classical dictionary this is the cocycle condition. -/
131	  coassoc (m : M) :
132	    (coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B (coaction m) =
133	      (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B (coaction m)
134	
135	namespace DescentDatum
136	
137	variable (A B) in
138	/-- The canonical descent datum on a base change `B ⊗[A] N`, with coaction
139	`b ⊗ₜ n ↦ b ⊗ₜ 1 ⊗ₜ n`. -/
140	@[simps coaction]
141	noncomputable def baseChange (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
142	    DescentDatum A B (B ⊗[A] N) where
143	  coaction := (TensorProduct.mk A B N 1).baseChange B
144	  counit x := by
145	    induction x with
146	    | zero => simp
147	    | tmul b n => simp [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
148	    | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
149	  coassoc x := by
150	    induction x with
151	    | zero => simp
152	    | tmul b n => simp
153	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
154	
155	variable (D : DescentDatum A B M)
156	
157	/-- The `A`-linear difference between the coaction and the canonical map `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`;
158	its kernel is the descended module. -/
159	def coactionSub : M →ₗ[A] B ⊗[A] M :=
160	  D.coaction.restrictScalars A - TensorProduct.mk A B M 1
161	
162	@[simp] theorem coactionSub_apply (m : M) : D.coactionSub m = D.coaction m - 1 ⊗ₜ m := rfl
163	
164	/-- The descended `A`-module of a descent datum: the equalizer
165	`M₀ = {m : M | δ m = 1 ⊗ₜ m}`. -/
166	def descended : Submodule A M := LinearMap.ker D.coactionSub
167	
168	theorem mem_descended {m : M} : m ∈ D.descended ↔ D.coaction m = 1 ⊗ₜ m := by
169	  rw [descended, LinearMap.mem_ker, coactionSub_apply, sub_eq_zero]
170	
171	/-- The canonical comparison map `B ⊗[A] M₀ →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.  Flat descent
172	(`comparison_bijective`) asserts this is an isomorphism when `B` is flat over `A`. -/
173	noncomputable def comparison : B ⊗[A] D.descended →ₗ[B] M :=
174	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B D.descended.subtype
175	
176	@[simp] theorem comparison_tmul (b : B) (m : D.descended) :
177	    D.comparison (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • (m : M) := rfl
178	
179	theorem comparison_eq_actionMap (x : B ⊗[A] D.descended) :
180	    D.comparison x = actionMap A B M (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B x) := by
181	  induction x with
182	  | zero => simp
183	  | tmul b m => simp
184	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
185	
186	private theorem coactionSub_lTensor_apply (x : B ⊗[A] M) :
187	    D.coactionSub.lTensor B x =
188	      (D.coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x -
189	        (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B x := by
190	  induction x with
191	  | zero => simp
192	  | tmul b m => simp [TensorProduct.tmul_sub]
193	  | add x y hx hy =>
194	      simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
195	      abel
196	
197	/-- The coaction retracts onto the kernel of `coactionSub ⊗ B`: any `x : B ⊗[A] M` on which
198	the two liftings agree is a coaction value, namely of `actionMap x`.  This is the
199	contracting-homotopy computation at the heart of both effectivity and Amitsur exactness. -/
200	theorem coaction_actionMap {x : B ⊗[A] M}
201	    (hx : (D.coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x =
202	      (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B x) :
203	    D.coaction (actionMap A B M x) = x :=
204	  (actionMap_baseChange D.coaction x).symm.trans <| by rw [hx, actionMap_baseChange_mk]
205	
206	/-- **Effectivity of flat descent for modules**: for `B` flat over `A`, the canonical map
207	`B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` out of the descended module is bijective. -/
208	theorem comparison_bijective [Module.Flat A B] : Function.Bijective D.comparison := by
209	  have hexact : Function.Exact (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B) (D.coactionSub.lTensor B) :=
210	    Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B D.coactionSub.exact_subtype_ker_map
211	  have hinj : Function.Injective (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B) :=
212	    Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ D.descended.injective_subtype
213	  have key : ∀ y : B ⊗[A] D.descended,
214	      D.coaction (D.comparison y) = D.descended.subtype.lTensor B y := by
215	    intro y
216	    rw [comparison_eq_actionMap]
217	    refine D.coaction_actionMap (sub_eq_zero.mp ?_)
218	    rw [← coactionSub_lTensor_apply]
219	    exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
220	  constructor
221	  · intro y z hyz
222	    exact hinj (by rw [← key, ← key, hyz])
223	  · intro m
224	    have hm : D.coactionSub.lTensor B (D.coaction m) = 0 := by
225	      rw [coactionSub_lTensor_apply, D.coassoc m, sub_self]
226	    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact _).mp hm
227	    refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
228	    have hcoact : D.coaction (D.comparison y) = D.coaction m := by rw [key y, hy]
229	    have := congrArg (actionMap A B M) hcoact
230	    rwa [D.counit, D.counit] at this
231	
232	/-- The comparison isomorphism `B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ₗ[B] M` of flat descent. -/
233	noncomputable def descentEquiv [Module.Flat A B] : B ⊗[A] D.descended ≃ₗ[B] M :=
234	  LinearEquiv.ofBijective D.comparison D.comparison_bijective
235	
236	@[simp] theorem descentEquiv_tmul [Module.Flat A B] (b : B) (m : D.descended) :
237	    D.descentEquiv (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • (m : M) := rfl
238	
239	section Amitsur
240	
241	variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
242	
243	/-- **Amitsur exactness in degrees `≤ 1`**: for a faithfully flat `A → B` and any
244	`A`-module `N`, the sequence `0 → N → B ⊗[A] N ⇉ B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] N` is exact; here the pair
245	of arrows is encoded by the single map `coactionSub` of the canonical descent datum, whose
246	kernel is the equalizer. -/
247	theorem exact_mk_coactionSub (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
248	    Function.Exact (TensorProduct.mk A B N 1) (baseChange A B N).coactionSub := by
249	  apply (Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_exact_iff_exact A B _ _).mp
250	  intro z
251	  constructor
252	  · intro hz
253	    refine ⟨actionMap A B (B ⊗[A] N) z, ?_⟩
254	    have hx := (baseChange A B N).coaction_actionMap (x := z) (sub_eq_zero.mp (by
255	      rw [← coactionSub_lTensor_apply]; exact hz))
256	    rw [baseChange_coaction] at hx
257	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
258	    exact hx
259	  · rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩
260	    rw [coactionSub_lTensor_apply, sub_eq_zero]
261	    induction x with
262	    | zero => simp
263	    | tmul b n => simp
264	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
265	
266	/-- The unit of descent: for a faithfully flat `A → B`, the canonical map identifies an
267	`A`-module `N` with the descended module of the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N`.
268	This is the degree `0` consequence of Amitsur exactness. -/
269	noncomputable def unitEquiv (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
270	    N ≃ₗ[A] (baseChange A B N).descended := by
271	  refine LinearEquiv.ofBijective
272	    ((TensorProduct.mk A B N 1).codRestrict (baseChange A B N).descended fun n => ?_)
273	    ⟨fun n n' h => ?_, fun y => ?_⟩
274	  · rw [mem_descended]
275	    simp
276	  · exact Module.FaithfullyFlat.tensorProduct_mk_injective (A := A) (B := B) N
277	      (congrArg Subtype.val h)
278	  · have h0 : (baseChange A B N).coactionSub (y : B ⊗[A] N) = 0 := LinearMap.mem_ker.mp y.2
279	    obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := (exact_mk_coactionSub N (y : B ⊗[A] N)).mp h0
280	    exact ⟨n, Subtype.ext hn⟩
281	
282	@[simp] theorem unitEquiv_apply_coe (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] (n : N) :
283	    (unitEquiv (A := A) (B := B) N n : B ⊗[A] N) = 1 ⊗ₜ n := rfl
284	
285	variable {N : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
286	
287	/-- **Uniqueness of descent**: if `N` is an `A`-module and `e : B ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[B] M`
288	intertwines the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N` with `D`, then `N` is canonically
289	`A`-isomorphic to the descended module of `D`.  In particular two descents of the same
290	datum are canonically isomorphic (compose one such equivalence with the inverse of the
291	other). -/
292	noncomputable def equivDescended (e : (B ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] M)
293	    (he : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] N,
294	      D.coaction (e x) = ((e : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] M).restrictScalars A).baseChange B
295	        ((baseChange A B N).coaction x)) :
296	    N ≃ₗ[A] D.descended := by
297	  refine (unitEquiv N).trans <|
298	    ((e.restrictScalars A).submoduleMap (baseChange A B N).descended).trans
299	      (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ ?_)
300	  have hinj : Function.Injective
301	      (((e : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] M).restrictScalars A).baseChange B) := by
302	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
303	    exact Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ e.injective
304	  ext m
305	  simp only [Submodule.mem_map]
306	  constructor
307	  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
308	    rw [mem_descended] at hx ⊢
309	    change D.coaction (e x) = 1 ⊗ₜ (e x)
310	    rw [he x, hx]
311	    simp
312	  · intro hm
313	    refine ⟨e.symm m, ?_, e.apply_symm_apply m⟩
314	    rw [mem_descended] at hm ⊢
315	    apply hinj
316	    have := he (e.symm m)
317	    rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply] at this
318	    rw [← this, hm]
319	    simp
320	
321	@[simp] theorem equivDescended_apply_coe (e : (B ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] M)
322	    (he : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] N,
323	      D.coaction (e x) = ((e : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] M).restrictScalars A).baseChange B
324	        ((baseChange A B N).coaction x)) (n : N) :
325	    (D.equivDescended e he n : M) = e (1 ⊗ₜ n) := rfl
326	
327	end Amitsur
328	
329	end DescentDatum
330	
331	end Module

14	/-!
15	# Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules
16	
17	Let `A → B` be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings.  This file shows that the
18	module-theoretic properties *finite*, *finitely presented*, *flat*, *projective* and
19	*invertible* all descend along `A → B`: if `B ⊗[A] P` has the property over `B`, then `P`
20	has it over `A`.  Combined with the effectivity theorem of
21	`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent` this yields: a `B`-module `M` with a descent
22	datum descends to an `A`-module `M₀` (unique up to canonical isomorphism), and if `M` is
23	invertible then so is `M₀`.
24	
25	The descent of invertibility is reduced, via the definition
26	`Module.Invertible R M ↔ Function.Bijective (contractLeft R M)`, to two ingredients:
27	
28	* the *dual base-change comparison* `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is an
29	  isomorphism for `P` finite projective (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`, proved by a
30	  retract argument from the finite free case, which is `IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight`);
31	* bijectivity of `A`-linear maps descends along faithfully flat maps
32	  (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective`).
33	
34	Finiteness and projectivity of `P` are themselves obtained by descent: mathlib provides
35	finiteness (`Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`) and flatness
36	(`Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`); we add finite presentation
37	(`Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`), and
38	projectivity follows from flat + finitely presented.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`:
43	  finite presentation descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
44	* `Module.Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: finite projectivity
45	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
46	* `Module.dualBaseChange A B P : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)`: the dual
47	  base-change comparison map.
48	* `Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`: the comparison map is bijective for finite projective
49	  `P` (over an arbitrary `A`-algebra `B`).
50	* `Module.Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: invertibility
51	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
52	* `Module.DescentDatum.finite_descended`, `…flat_descended`,
53	  `…finitePresentation_descended`, `…projective_descended`,
54	  `…invertible_descended`: for a descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to a
55	  faithfully flat `A → B`, the descended module inherits each property from `M`;
56	  in particular **an invertible module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
57	  module**.
58	
59	All modules live in a single universe `u`.
60	-/
61	
62	universe u
63	
64	open TensorProduct
65	
66	namespace Module
67	
68	variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]

70	/-! ### Descent of finite presentation -/
71	
72	/-- Finite presentation of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
73	theorem FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
74	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
75	    [Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
76	    Module.FinitePresentation A P := by
77	  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
78	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
79	  obtain ⟨n, p, hp⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
80	  have hpB : Function.Surjective (p.baseChange B) := by
81	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
82	    exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective B hp
83	  have hker : (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)).FG :=
84	    Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker (p.baseChange B) hpB
85	  have hexact := Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B p.exact_subtype_ker_map
86	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B) := by
87	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
88	    exact Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _
89	      (LinearMap.ker p).injective_subtype
90	  have hrange : LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B)
91	      = LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) := by
92	    ext x
93	    rw [LinearMap.mem_range, LinearMap.mem_ker]
94	    constructor
95	    · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩
96	      simp only [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
97	      exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
98	    · intro hx
99	      rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hx
100	      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact x).mp hx
101	      exact ⟨y, by rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]; exact hy⟩
102	  have e : (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) ≃ₗ[B] LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) :=
103	    (LinearEquiv.ofInjective _ hinj).trans (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ hrange)
104	  have : Module.Finite B (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)) := Module.Finite.iff_fg.mpr hker
105	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) := Module.Finite.equiv e.symm
106	  have : Module.Finite A (LinearMap.ker p) :=
107	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
108	  exact Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective p hp (Module.Finite.iff_fg.mp this)
109	
110	/-- Finite projectivity of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
111	theorem Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
112	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
113	    [Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] P)] [Projective B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
114	    Projective A P := by
115	  have : Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
116	    Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B (B ⊗[A] P)
117	  have : Module.FinitePresentation A P :=
118	    FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B P
119	  have : Module.Flat A P := Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct A P B
120	  exact Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation (R := A) (M := P)

122	/-! ### The dual base-change comparison map -/
123	
124	section DualBaseChange
125	
126	variable {A B} in
127	/-- Two `B`-functionals on `B ⊗[A] X` that agree on the tensors `1 ⊗ₜ x` are equal. -/
128	private theorem dual_ext {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
129	    {F G : Dual B (B ⊗[A] X)} (h : ∀ x : X, F (1 ⊗ₜ x) = G (1 ⊗ₜ x)) : F = G := by
130	  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
131	  apply TensorProduct.ext'
132	  intro b x
133	  have hb : b ⊗ₜ[A] x = b • (1 ⊗ₜ[A] x : B ⊗[A] X) := by
134	    rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
135	  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, hb, map_smul, h]
136	
137	variable (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
138	
139	/-- The canonical `B`-linear comparison map from the base change of the dual to the dual
140	of the base change, `b ⊗ₜ f ↦ b • (f.baseChange B)`.  It is bijective for finite
141	projective `P` (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`). -/
142	noncomputable def dualBaseChange : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
143	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (Module.Dual.baseChange B)
144	
145	@[simp] theorem dualBaseChange_tmul (b : B) (f : Dual A P) :
146	    dualBaseChange A B P (b ⊗ₜ f) = b • Module.Dual.baseChange B f := rfl
147	
148	/-- Naturality of the dual base-change comparison map. -/

/-!

# Being projective is a local property

## Main results
- `LinearMap.split_surjective_of_localization_maximal`
  If `N` is finitely presented, then `f : M →ₗ[R] N`
  being split injective can be checked on stalks (of maximal ideals).
- `Module.projective_of_localization_maximal` If `M` is finitely presented,
  then `M` being projective can be checked on stalks (of maximal ideals).

## TODO
- Show that being projective is Zariski-local (very hard)

-/

universe uM

variable {R N N' : Type*} {M : Type uM} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N]

theorem Module.free_of_isLocalizedModule {Rₛ Mₛ} [AddCommGroup Mₛ] [Module R Mₛ]
    [CommRing Rₛ] [Algebra R Rₛ] [Module Rₛ Mₛ] [IsScalarTower R Rₛ Mₛ]
    (S) (f : M →ₗ[R] Mₛ) [IsLocalization S Rₛ] [IsLocalizedModule S f] [Module.Free R M] :
    Module.Free Rₛ Mₛ :=
  Free.of_equiv (IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange S Rₛ f).equiv

Also see `IsLocalizedModule.lift_rank_eq` for a version for non-free modules,
but requires `S` to not contain any zero-divisors.

theorem Module.lift_rank_of_isLocalizedModule_of_free
    (Rₛ : Type uR') {Mₛ : Type uM'} [AddCommGroup Mₛ] [Module R Mₛ]
    [CommRing Rₛ] [Algebra R Rₛ] [Module Rₛ Mₛ] [IsScalarTower R Rₛ Mₛ] (S : Submonoid R)
    (f : M →ₗ[R] Mₛ) [IsLocalization S Rₛ] [IsLocalizedModule S f] [Module.Free R M]
    [Nontrivial Rₛ] :
    Cardinal.lift.{uM} (Module.rank Rₛ Mₛ) = Cardinal.lift.{uM'} (Module.rank R M) := by
  apply Cardinal.lift_injective.{max uM' uR'}
  have := (algebraMap R Rₛ).domain_nontrivial
  have := (IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange S Rₛ f).equiv.lift_rank_eq.symm
  simp only [rank_tensorProduct, rank_self,
    Cardinal.lift_one, one_mul, Cardinal.lift_lift] at this ⊢
  convert! this

data.content:
A module `M` over a commutative ring `R` is *faithfully flat* if it is flat and,
for all `R`-linear maps `f : N → N'` such that `id ⊗ f = 0`, we have `f = 0`.
-/
@[mk_iff] class FaithfullyFlat : Prop extends Module.Flat R M where
  submodule_ne_top : ∀ ⦃m : Ideal R⦄ (_ : Ideal.IsMaximal m), m • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤

namespace FaithfullyFlat
instance self : FaithfullyFlat R R where
  submodule_ne_top m h r := Ideal.eq_top_iff_one _ |>.not.1 h.ne_top <| by
    simpa using show 1 ∈ (m • ⊤ : Ideal R) from r.symm ▸ ⟨⟩

section proper_ideal

lemma iff_flat_and_proper_ideal :
    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔
    (Flat R M ∧ ∀ (I : Ideal R), I ≠ ⊤ → I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤) := by
  rw [faithfullyFlat_iff]
  refine ⟨fun ⟨flat, h⟩ => ⟨flat, fun I hI r => ?_⟩, fun h => ⟨h.1, fun m hm => h.2 _ hm.ne_top⟩⟩
  obtain ⟨m, hm, le⟩ := I.exists_le_maximal hI
  exact h hm <| eq_top_iff.2 <| show ⊤ ≤ m • ⊤ from r ▸ Submodule.smul_mono le (by simp [r])

lemma iff_flat_and_ideal_smul_eq_top :
    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔
    (Flat R M ∧ ∀ (I : Ideal R), I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) = ⊤ → I = ⊤) :=
  iff_flat_and_proper_ideal R M |>.trans <| and_congr_right_iff.2 fun _ => iff_of_eq <|
    forall_congr fun I => eq_iff_iff.2 <| by tauto

end proper_ideal

section faithful

instance rTensor_nontrivial
    [fl : FaithfullyFlat R M] (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Nontrivial N] :
    Nontrivial (N ⊗[R] M) := by
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := nontrivial_iff_exists_ne (0 : N) |>.1 inferInstance
  let I := (Submodule.span R {n}).annihilator
  by_cases I_ne_top : I = ⊤
  · rw [Ideal.eq_top_iff_one, Submodule.mem_annihilator_span_singleton, one_smul] at I_ne_top
    contradiction
  let inc : R ⧸ I →ₗ[R] N := Submodule.liftQ _ ((LinearMap.lsmul R N).flip n) <| fun r hr => by
    simpa only [LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.flip_apply, LinearMap.lsmul_apply,
      Submodule.mem_annihilator_span_singleton, I] using hr
  have injective_inc : Function.Injective inc := LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.1 <| eq_bot_iff.2 <| by
    intro r hr
    induction r using Quotient.inductionOn' with | h r =>
    simpa only [Submodule.Quotient.mk''_eq_mk, Submodule.mem_bot, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero,
      Submodule.mem_annihilator_span_singleton, LinearMap.mem_ker, Submodule.liftQ_apply,
      LinearMap.flip_apply, LinearMap.lsmul_apply, I, inc] using hr
  have ne_top := iff_flat_and_proper_ideal R M |>.1 fl |>.2 I I_ne_top
  refine subsingleton_or_nontrivial _ |>.resolve_left fun rid => ne_top ?_
  rw [← Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff]
  exact (fl.toFlat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap inc injective_inc).comp
    (quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I).symm.injective |>.subsingleton

instance lTensor_nontrivial
    [FaithfullyFlat R M] (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Nontrivial N] :
    Nontrivial (M ⊗[R] N) :=
  TensorProduct.comm R M N |>.toEquiv.nontrivial

lemma rTensor_reflects_triviality
    [FaithfullyFlat R M] (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    [h : Subsingleton (N ⊗[R] M)] : Subsingleton N := by

    [FaithfullyFlat R M] (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]

    Subsingleton N := by

is a linear map whose localization at a prime ideal `p` is bijective, then there exists

lemma Module.FinitePresentation.exists_notMem_bijective [Module.Finite R M]
    [Module.FinitePresentation R N] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] {Mₚ Nₚ : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup Mₚ] [AddCommGroup Nₚ] [Module R Mₚ] [Module R Nₚ]
    (fM : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ) (fN : N →ₗ[R] Nₚ)
    [IsLocalizedModule p.primeCompl fM] [IsLocalizedModule p.primeCompl fN]
    (hf : Function.Bijective (IsLocalizedModule.map p.primeCompl fM fN f)) :
    ∃ (g : R), g ∉ p ∧ Function.Bijective (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers g) f) := by
  obtain ⟨g, hg, h⟩ := exists_bijective_map_powers p.primeCompl fM fN f hf

Any `Mₛ ≃ₗ[R] Nₛ` between the localizations at `S : Submonoid R` can be lifted to an
isomorphism between `Mᵣ ≃ₗ[R] Nᵣ` for some `r ∈ S`.

lemma Module.FinitePresentation.exists_lift_equiv_of_isLocalizedModule

    (l : M' ≃ₗ[R] N') :
    ∃ (r : R) (hr : r ∈ S)

        LocalizedModule.Away r N),
      (LocalizedModule.lift (.powers r) g fun s ↦ map_units g ⟨s.1, SetLike.le_def.mp
        (Submonoid.powers_le.mpr hr) s.2⟩) ∘ₗ l'.toLinearMap =

theorem exists_basicOpen_le {V : X.Opens} (x : V) (h : ↑x ∈ U) :
    ∃ f : Γ(X, U), X.basicOpen f ≤ V ∧ ↑x ∈ X.basicOpen f := by
  have : IsAffine _ := hU
  obtain ⟨_, ⟨_, ⟨r, rfl⟩, rfl⟩, h₁, h₂ : _ ≤ U.ι ⁻¹ᵁ V⟩ :=
    (isBasis_basicOpen U).exists_subset_of_mem_open (x.2 : (⟨x, h⟩ : U) ∈ _) (U.ι ⁻¹ᵁ V).isOpen
  replace h₁ : x.1 ∈ X.basicOpen r := by simpa [U.mem_basicOpen_toScheme] using! h₁
  replace h₂ : X.basicOpen r ≤ V := by
    simpa [Scheme.image_basicOpen] using! (U.ι.image_mono h₂).trans (U.ι.image_preimage_le _)
  exact ⟨U.topIso.hom.hom r, by simp [Scheme.Opens.toScheme_presheaf_obj, h₁, h₂]⟩

noncomputable
instance {R : CommRingCat} {U} : Algebra R Γ(Spec R, U) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Algebra R ((Spec.structureSheaf R).presheaf.obj _))

@[simp]
lemma algebraMap_Spec_obj {R : CommRingCat} {U} : algebraMap R Γ(Spec R, U) =
    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).inv ≫ (Spec R).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op).hom := rfl

instance {R : CommRingCat} {f : R} :
    IsLocalization.Away f Γ(Spec R, PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsLocalization.Away f
    ((Spec.structureSheaf R).obj.obj (op <| PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)))

/-- Given an affine open U and some `f : U`,
this is the canonical map `Γ(𝒪ₓ, D(f)) ⟶ Γ(Spec 𝒪ₓ(U), D(f))`
This is an isomorphism, as witnessed by an `IsIso` instance. -/
def basicOpenSectionsToAffine :
    Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) ⟶ Γ(Spec Γ(X, U), PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) :=
  hU.fromSpec.app (X.basicOpen f) ≫
    (Spec Γ(X, U)).presheaf.map (eqToHom (hU.fromSpec_preimage_basicOpen f).symm).op

instance basicOpenSectionsToAffine_isIso :
    IsIso (basicOpenSectionsToAffine hU f) :=
  (hU.fromSpec.isIso_app _ (hU.opensRange_fromSpec.symm ▸ X.basicOpen_le f)).comp_isIso'
    inferInstance

include hU in
theorem isLocalization_basicOpen :
    IsLocalization.Away f Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) := by
  apply
    (IsLocalization.isLocalization_iff_of_ringEquiv (Submonoid.powers f)
      (asIso <| basicOpenSectionsToAffine hU f).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv).mpr
  convert! StructureSheaf.IsLocalization.to_basicOpen _ f using 1
  apply Algebra.algebra_ext
  intro _
  congr 1
  dsimp [CommRingCat.ofHom, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, ← CommRingCat.hom_comp,
    basicOpenSectionsToAffine]
  rw [hU.fromSpec.naturality_assoc, hU.fromSpec_app_self]
  rfl

instance _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalization_away_of_isAffine
    [IsAffine X] (r : Γ(X, ⊤)) :

/-- Localizing the localization of `R` at `x` at the image of `y` is the same as localizing
`R` at `y * x`. See `IsLocalization.Away.mul'` for the `x * y` version. -/
lemma mul (T : Type*) [CommSemiring T] [Algebra S T]
    [Algebra R T] [IsScalarTower R S T] (x y : R)
    [IsLocalization.Away x S] [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap R S y) T] :
    IsLocalization.Away (y * x) T := by
  refine mk _ ?_ (fun z ↦ ?_) (fun a b h ↦ ?_)
  · simp only [map_mul, IsUnit.mul_iff, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply R S T]
    exact ⟨algebraMap_isUnit _, IsUnit.map _ (algebraMap_isUnit x)⟩
  · obtain ⟨m, p, hpq⟩ := surj (algebraMap R S y) z
    obtain ⟨n, a, hab⟩ := surj x p
    use m + n, a * x ^ m * y ^ n
    simp only [mul_pow, pow_add, map_pow, map_mul, ← mul_assoc, hpq,
      IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply R S T, ← hab]
    ring
  · repeat rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply R S T] at h
    obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_of_eq (algebraMap R S y) h
    simp only [← map_pow, ← map_mul, ← map_mul] at hn
    obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := exists_of_eq x hn
    use n + m
    convert_to y ^ m * x ^ n * (x ^ m * (y ^ n * a)) = y ^ m * x ^ n * (x ^ m * (y ^ n * b))
    · ring
    · ring
    · rw [hm]

/-- Localizing the localization of `R` at `x` at the image of `y` is the same as localizing
`R` at `x * y`. See `IsLocalization.Away.mul` for the `y * x` version. -/
lemma mul' (T : Type*) [CommSemiring T] [Algebra S T] [Algebra R T] [IsScalarTower R S T] (x y : R)
    [IsLocalization.Away x S] [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap R S y) T] :
    IsLocalization.Away (x * y) T :=
  mul_comm x y ▸ mul S T x y

/-- Localizing the localization of `R` at `x` at the image of `y` is the same as localizing
`R` at `y * x`. -/
instance (x y : R) [IsLocalization.Away x S] :
    IsLocalization.Away (y * x) (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S y)) :=
  IsLocalization.Away.mul S (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S y)) _ _

/-- Localizing the localization of `R` at `x` at the image of `y` is the same as localizing
`R` at `x * y`. -/
instance (x y : R) [IsLocalization.Away x S] :
    IsLocalization.Away (x * y) (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S y)) :=
  IsLocalization.Away.mul' S (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S y)) _ _

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.overSpecMap f`: `Spec` of a `k`-algebra map `f : A →ₐ[k] B`, as a
  morphism `overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A` of `Over (Spec k)`, strictly functorial

* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap C f`: restriction of relative Picard classes along
  `Spec f`, a group homomorphism `relPic C (overSpec k A) →* relPic C (overSpec k B)`,
  covariantly functorial in the algebra (`relPicAlgMap_id`, `relPicAlgMap_comp`).

The étale plus construction (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean`) consumes only this interface: descent
classes on an étale cover are an equalizer of two `relPicAlgMap`s, and all refinement
transports are `relPicAlgMap`s of `A`-algebra maps restricted to `k`.

# The affine dictionary `X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)` — design (run 0027, s0018)

Item-5 of the Wave-3 Picard design (`wave3-picard-design.md` §4.4): the missing brick between
the definitional Čech Picard group and mathlib's `CommRing.Pic`.  We prove it for an
arbitrary **affine scheme** `X` against `A := Γ(X, ⊤)` — no `Spec R`/`ΓSpecIso` plumbing in
the core construction; consumers specialize `X := Spec R`.  (This is literally a TODO in
mathlib's `RingTheory/PicardGroup.lean`: "Exhibit isomorphism with sheaf cohomology
`H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`" — everything below is built PR-shaped.)

## Route (Čech class → invertible module): Zariski descent along a basic cover

A unit Čech cocycle `γ` on a pointed cover `𝒰` of affine `X` is converted into a
**descent datum on the free rank-1 module** over the faithfully flat `A`-algebra
`B := ∏ i, Γ(X, X.basicOpen (r i))` for a finite covering family of basic opens refining
`𝒰`, and descended to an invertible `A`-module by the landed brick-4
(`Descent/ModuleDescent.lean` + `Descent/InvertibleModule.lean`).  No sheaf-theoretic
"twisted glued sections" module is ever constructed; localization algebra does everything.

Layers (each a file):

1. **`Descent/UnitDescent.lean`** (pure algebra).  For a unit `u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` define
   `Module.IsDescentCocycle u` (normalization `lmul' u = 1` + cocycle identity via the three
   inclusions `B ⊗ B → B ⊗ B ⊗ B`), the comodule-form datum `DescentDatum.ofUnit`
   (coaction `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`), and the descended submodule `hu.descended ⊆ B` with the
   full calculus, everything up to canonical `A`-module iso:
   * `descended 1 ≃ A` (Amitsur degree 0);
   * coboundary invariance `descended (ι₂β · ι₁β⁻¹ · u) ≃ descended u` (elementary: `β •`);
   * `descended u ⊗ descended v ≃ descended (u·v)` (via `equivDescended` against
     `distribBaseChange` + the two `descentEquiv`s; datum check is ring algebra on tensors);
   * base-change functoriality along any `h : B →ₐ[A] B'` of faithfully flat algebras:
     `descended u ≃ descended ((h ⊗ h) u)` (via `cancelBaseChange`);
   * triviality: `descended u ≅ A → u = ι₂β · ι₁β⁻¹` for the unit `β = m₀`, where `m₀` is
     the image of `1`; bijectivity of `(· * m₀)` comes from `descentEquiv`, so `m₀ ∈ Bˣ`.
   * Pic-level wrappers `IsDescentCocycle.picClass : CommRing.Pic A` + the four laws.

2. **`Algebra/PiLocalization.lean`** (pure algebra, generic).  For a finite family of
   `A`-algebras `S i` with `IsLocalization.Away (f i) (S i)`:
   * **the pi-ext lemma**: two `A`-algebra maps `(∀ i, S i) →ₐ[A] C` agreeing on the
     idempotents `Pi.single i 1` are equal.  Proof: `Φᵢ := (quotient by span{1 - φ(eᵢ)}) ∘
     φ(single i ·)` is a *unital* `A`-algebra map out of the localization `S i`, so unique
     (`IsLocalization.ringHom_ext`); multiply the resulting congruence by the idempotent.
     This single lemma discharges every transport identity below — no naturality diagrams.
   * `Module.FaithfullyFlat A (∀ i, S i)` when `Ideal.span (range f) = ⊤` (flat: finite
     product of localizations; faithful: `iff_flat_and_proper_ideal`, a maximal `m` misses
     some `f i`, and `m`-extension stays proper in `S i`).
   * `AlgEquiv`s `(∀ i, S i) ⊗[A] (∀ j, T j) ≃ₐ[A] ∀ p : ι × κ, S p.1 ⊗[A] T p.2`
     (finite `TensorProduct.piRight` twice, ring structure by tensor induction) and the
     component upgrade `S ⊗[A] T ≃ₐ[A] C` for `[Away f S] [Away g T] [Away (f*g) C]`
     (`IsLocalization.tensor` + `Submonoid.map_powers` + `IsLocalization.Away.mul'` +
     `IsLocalization.algEquiv`); canonical maps `Away.algHomOfDvd (f ∣ g) : S_f →ₐ[A] S_g`;
     `Subsingleton (S →ₐ[A] C)` for localizations makes all choices canonical.

3. **`Algebra/LocalizationCocycle.lean`**: packaging.  Given units
   `γ p ∈ (T p.1 p.2)ˣ` on the double overlaps with (i) diagonal normalization in `S i` and
   (ii) the cocycle identity in the triple overlaps `W i j k` (all maps the canonical ones),
   produce `cocycleUnit γ ∈ (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` (via the layer-2 equivalences) with
   `IsDescentCocycle`, plus: multiplicativity in `γ`, coboundary detection
   (`cocycleUnit γ = descentCoboundary β ↔` componentwise), and refinement transport along
   `τ : ι' → ι` with `f (τ i') ∣-up-to-radical f' i'`.  All verified through the pi-ext
   lemma by evaluating on idempotents (`doubleEquiv (eᵢ ⊗ eⱼ) = single (i,j) 1` is forced).

4. **`Picard/PicAffine.lean`** (the dictionary).  For affine `X`:
   `CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`.
   * Choices per class: pointed basic refinement `x ∈ D(r x) ≤ 𝒰 x`
     (`IsAffineOpen.exists_basicOpen_le`), finite subcover `σ : Fin n → X` (compactness),
     `γ̃ (i,j) := unitsEvInf γ (σ i) (σ j)` restricted to `Γ(X, X.basicOpen (rᵢ * rⱼ))`
     (`Scheme.basicOpen_mul`); conditions (i),(ii) from `unitsEvInf_trans`.
   * Well-definedness: a single master comparison — enlarge the finite family
     (map-transport along an index inclusion), refine both packages to the common pointed
     refinement `𝒰₁ ⊓ 𝒰₂` with `r x := r₁ x * r₂ x`, where the H¹ classes agree, hence the
     cocycles are cohomologous and layer-1 coboundary invariance finishes.  All comparisons
     evaluate `γ` at the *same pairs of points*, so no cross-point cocycle juggling occurs.
   * Injectivity: `picClass = 1` gives componentwise `β i ∈ Γ(X, D i)ˣ`; the general-family
     glued-coboundary lemma (generalizing `exists_glued_coboundary` from
     `RefinementInjectivity.lean` to an arbitrary finite refining family) rebuilds a
     coboundary on `𝒰` itself; conclude with `CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff`.
   * Surjectivity (Phase 2 of the dictionary, may slip a session): invertible `M` is
     finite projective (mathlib), trivializes on a basic cover by
     `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_lift_equiv_of_isLocalizedModule` at each prime +
     `Pic (local ring) = 0`; transition cocycle → class; `toPic` of it is `Pic.mk A M` by
     descent uniqueness (`equivDescended`).  Then `cechPicEquivPic : X.CechPic ≃* Pic Γ(X,⊤)`
     and naturality in `X` (next session, needed by the (C1) assembly).

## Why this route (vs. glued-sections module)

Localizing an equalizer submodule of an infinite product (pointed covers have one open per
point!) needs finite-subcover surgery *inside* every localization argument; the descent
route quarantines quasi-compactness into a single choice of finite basic subcover and
reuses the landed effectivity/uniqueness/invertibility bricks unchanged.  The extra cost —
`B ⊗[A] B ≃ ∏ (double overlaps)` — is pure `IsLocalization` bookkeeping, and every identity
between maps out of localizations is *free* (`Subsingleton`-style uniqueness + idempotent
evaluation), which is exactly what makes the cocycle-condition transport tractable in Lean.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.InvertibleModule

/-!
# Descent data from unit 1-cocycles, and the Picard class of a cocycle

Let `A → B` be a map of commutative rings.  A **descent 1-cocycle** is a unit
`u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` that is normalized along the multiplication `B ⊗[A] B → B` and satisfies
the 1-cocycle identity in `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] B` (`Module.IsDescentCocycle`).  Such a unit
twists the trivial descent datum on the `B`-module `B`: the coaction `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`
is a descent datum in the comodule form of `AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent`
(`Module.DescentDatum.ofUnit`), so for faithfully flat `A → B` it descends to an invertible
`A`-module `hu.descended` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.InvertibleModule`), whose class in
mathlib's Picard group is `hu.picClass : CommRing.Pic A`.

This file develops the full calculus of `picClass`, which is the algebraic heart of the
dictionary between the Čech Picard group of an affine scheme and `CommRing.Pic`
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine`):

* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_one`: the trivial cocycle has trivial class.
* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_mul`: `picClass` is multiplicative in the cocycle.
* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_descentCoboundary_mul`: `picClass` is invariant under
  multiplication by the coboundary `β ↦ (1 ⊗ β) * (β ⊗ 1)⁻¹` of a unit `β : Bˣ`.
* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_map`: `picClass` is invariant under base change of the
  cocycle along a map `h : B →ₐ[A] B'` of faithfully flat `A`-algebras.
* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_eq_one_iff`: the class is trivial **iff** the cocycle
  is a coboundary.

Everything is pinned to a single universe `u`, matching
`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent`.
-/

universe u

open TensorProduct

namespace Module

variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]

/-! ## The simplicial ring maps in low degrees -/

/-- The first-factor inclusion `B → B ⊗[A] B`, `b ↦ b ⊗ₜ 1`. -/
abbrev descentIncl₁ : B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] B := Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft

/-- The second-factor inclusion `B → B ⊗[A] B`, `b ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ b`. -/
abbrev descentIncl₂ : B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] B := Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight

/-- The face map `B ⊗[A] B → B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` hitting tensor positions `1, 2`:
`x ⊗ₜ y ↦ x ⊗ₜ (y ⊗ₜ 1)`. -/
noncomputable abbrev descentFace₁₂ : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A B) Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft

/-- The face map `B ⊗[A] B → B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` hitting tensor positions `1, 3`:
`x ⊗ₜ y ↦ x ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ y)`. -/
noncomputable abbrev descentFace₁₃ : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A B) Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight

/-- The face map `B ⊗[A] B → B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` hitting tensor positions `2, 3`:
`w ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ w`. -/
abbrev descentFace₂₃ : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight

variable {A B}

@[simp]
lemma descentIncl₁_apply (b : B) : descentIncl₁ A B b = b ⊗ₜ 1 := rfl

@[simp]
lemma descentIncl₂_apply (b : B) : descentIncl₂ A B b = 1 ⊗ₜ b := rfl

@[simp]
lemma descentFace₁₂_tmul (x y : B) : descentFace₁₂ A B (x ⊗ₜ y) = x ⊗ₜ (y ⊗ₜ 1) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma descentFace₁₃_tmul (x y : B) : descentFace₁₃ A B (x ⊗ₜ y) = x ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ y) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma descentFace₂₃_apply (w : B ⊗[A] B) : descentFace₂₃ A B w = 1 ⊗ₜ w := rfl

/-! ## Descent 1-cocycles -/

/-- A **descent 1-cocycle** relative to `A → B`: a unit of `B ⊗[A] B`, normalized along
the multiplication map, satisfying the 1-cocycle identity in `B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)`.  For
`B = ∏ i, A_{fᵢ}` a finite product of localizations covering `Spec A`, this is exactly a
Čech 1-cocycle of units on the cover by the basic opens `D(fᵢ)`. -/
structure IsDescentCocycle (u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ) : Prop where
  /-- Normalization: the multiplication `B ⊗[A] B → B` sends the cocycle to `1`. -/
  lmul'_eq_one : Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) u.val = 1
  /-- The 1-cocycle identity. -/
  cocycle : descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B u.val = descentFace₁₃ A B u.val

/-- The trivial unit is a descent cocycle. -/
theorem IsDescentCocycle.one : IsDescentCocycle (1 : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ) where
  lmul'_eq_one := by simp
  cocycle := by simp

/-- Descent cocycles are closed under multiplication. -/
theorem IsDescentCocycle.mul {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) : IsDescentCocycle (u * v) where
  lmul'_eq_one := by
    rw [Units.val_mul, map_mul, hu.lmul'_eq_one, hv.lmul'_eq_one, one_mul]
  cocycle := by
    simp only [Units.val_mul, map_mul]
    rw [show descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₂₃ A B v.val *
          (descentFace₁₂ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B v.val)
        = descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B u.val *
          (descentFace₂₃ A B v.val * descentFace₁₂ A B v.val) by ring]
    rw [hu.cocycle, hv.cocycle]

/-! ## The descent datum of a cocycle -/

variable (u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ)

variable (A B) in
/-- The coaction `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)` associated with a unit of `B ⊗[A] B`, as a `B`-linear
map (with `B` acting on the left tensor factor of the target). -/
noncomputable def unitCoaction : B →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] B where
  toFun x := u.val * x ⊗ₜ 1
  map_add' x y := by rw [add_tmul, mul_add]
  map_smul' b x := by
    rw [RingHom.id_apply, smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, ← mul_smul_comm, smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul,
      mul_one, mul_tmul_one_eq?]
    sorry

@[simp]
lemma unitCoaction_apply (x : B) : unitCoaction A B u x = u.val * x ⊗ₜ 1 := rfl

/-- The action map `B ⊗[A] B →ₗ[B] B` of `ModuleDescent` is the multiplication map. -/
lemma actionMap_eq_lmul' (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
    actionMap A B B w = Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) w := by
  induction w with
  | zero => simp
  | tmul b m => simp [smul_eq_mul]
  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]

/-- The base change to `B` of the coaction is left multiplication by `1 ⊗ₜ u` composed
with the face map `descentFace₁₂`. -/
lemma baseChange_unitCoaction (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
    ((unitCoaction A B u).restrictScalars A).baseChange B w
      = descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B w := by
  induction w with
  | zero => simp
  | tmul y z => sorry
    -- LHS = `y ⊗ₜ (u * (z ⊗ₜ 1))`; RHS = `(1 ⊗ₜ u) * (y ⊗ₜ (z ⊗ₜ 1))`, equal by
    -- `Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul` and `one_mul`.
  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy, mul_add]

/-- The base change to `B` of `x ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ x` is the face map `descentFace₁₃`. -/
lemma baseChange_mk_one (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
    (TensorProduct.mk A B B 1).baseChange B w = descentFace₁₃ A B w := by
  induction w with
  | zero => simp
  | tmul y z => rfl
  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]

/-- The descent datum on the `B`-module `B` associated with a descent 1-cocycle: the
coaction is `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`; counitality is the normalization and coassociativity is
the cocycle identity. -/
noncomputable def DescentDatum.ofUnit (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : DescentDatum A B B where
  coaction := unitCoaction A B u
  counit m := by
    rw [unitCoaction_apply, actionMap_eq_lmul', map_mul, hu.lmul'_eq_one, one_mul,
      Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'_apply_tmul, mul_one]
  coassoc m := by
    rw [unitCoaction_apply, baseChange_unitCoaction, baseChange_mk_one, map_mul,
      ← mul_assoc, hu.cocycle, map_mul]
    congr 1
    -- `descentFace₁₂ (m ⊗ₜ 1) = m ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ 1) = descentFace₁₃ (m ⊗ₜ 1)`
    rfl

/-- The descended `A`-module of a descent 1-cocycle: the submodule of `x : B` with
`u * (x ⊗ₜ 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ x`. -/
noncomputable def IsDescentCocycle.descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
    Submodule A B :=
  (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descended

lemma IsDescentCocycle.mem_descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) {m : B} :
    m ∈ hu.descended ↔ u.val * m ⊗ₜ 1 = 1 ⊗ₜ m :=
  DescentDatum.mem_descended _

/-! ## The Picard class of a cocycle -/

section picClass

variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]

/-- The descended module of a descent cocycle along a faithfully flat `A → B` is an
invertible `A`-module. -/
instance IsDescentCocycle.invertible_descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : Module.Invertible A hu.descended :=
  (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).invertible_descended

/-- The class in the Picard group of `A` of the module descended from a descent
1-cocycle relative to a faithfully flat `A → B`. -/
noncomputable def IsDescentCocycle.picClass {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : CommRing.Pic A :=
  CommRing.Pic.mk A hu.descended

/-- The descended module of the trivial cocycle is `A` itself (Amitsur exactness in
degree `0`). -/
noncomputable def descendedOneEquiv : (IsDescentCocycle.one (A := A) (B := B)).descended ≃ₗ[A] A := by
  -- Route: `(DescentDatum.ofUnit 1 .one).equivDescended e he |>.symm` with
  -- `e : B ⊗[A] A ≃ₗ[B] B := AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B`; the compatibility `he` is the

  -- tensors, extended by linearity via `TensorProduct.induction_on`.
  sorry

@[simp]
theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_one :
    (IsDescentCocycle.one (A := A) (B := B)).picClass = 1 :=
  CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff.mpr ⟨descendedOneEquiv⟩

/-- The descended module is multiplicative in the cocycle: `descended (u * v)` is the
tensor product of `descended u` and `descended v`. -/
noncomputable def descendedMulEquiv {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) :
    (hu.descended ⊗[A] hv.descended) ≃ₗ[A] (hu.mul hv).descended := by
  -- Route: `equivDescended (DescentDatum.ofUnit (u*v) (hu.mul hv)) e he` where
  -- `e : B ⊗[A] (M ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] B` is the composite
  -- `AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange` ≪≫ congr (descentEquiv hu) (descentEquiv hv)
  --   ≪≫ (B ⊗[B] B ≃ B)`,

  -- `(u*v) * (b*m*n ⊗ₜ 1) = (b ⊗ₜ 1) * (u * (m ⊗ₜ 1)) * (v * (n ⊗ₜ 1))

  -- using `hu.mem_descended`/`hv.mem_descended` for the members `m, n`.
  sorry

@[simp]
theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_mul {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) :
    (hu.mul hv).picClass = hu.picClass * hv.picClass := by
  rw [picClass, picClass, picClass, ← CommRing.Pic.mk_tensor]
  exact CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(descendedMulEquiv hu hv).symm⟩

end picClass

/-! ## Coboundaries -/

variable (A B) in
/-- The descent coboundary of a unit `β : Bˣ`: the unit `(1 ⊗ₜ β) * (β ⊗ₜ 1)⁻¹` of
`B ⊗[A] B`. -/
noncomputable def descentCoboundary (β : Bˣ) : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ :=
  Units.map (descentIncl₂ A B).toRingHom.toMonoidHom β
    * (Units.map (descentIncl₁ A B).toRingHom.toMonoidHom β)⁻¹

lemma descentCoboundary_val (β : Bˣ) :
    (descentCoboundary A B β).val = (1 ⊗ₜ β.val) * ((β⁻¹).val ⊗ₜ 1) := rfl

theorem isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary (β : Bˣ) :
    IsDescentCocycle (descentCoboundary A B β) where

    -- `descentFace₁₂ c = j₂β * (j₁β)⁻¹`, `descentFace₁₃ c = j₃β * (j₁β)⁻¹`, and the

    sorry

twist is `m ↦ β * m`. -/
noncomputable def descendedCoboundaryMulEquiv (β : Bˣ) {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}

import Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.Localization
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.Away.Basic
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.BaseChange
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Pi
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.DFinsupp

/-!
# Finite products of localizations of a commutative ring

For a commutative ring `A` and a finite covering family of basic opens — elements
`f i : A` with `Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤` — the product `∀ i, S i` of localizations
`S i := A[1/f i]` is the algebraic incarnation of a finite affine cover of `Spec A`.  This
file provides the toolkit used by the Čech–Picard dictionary
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine`) to run faithfully flat descent along such covers:

* `AlgHom.ext_of_isLocalization_pi` — **the pi-ext lemma**: two `A`-algebra maps out of a
  finite product of localizations of `A` agreeing on the coordinate idempotents
  `Pi.single i 1` are equal.  This makes every diagram of algebra maps out of such
  products commute by pure bookkeeping, replacing all naturality arguments downstream.
* `Module.FaithfullyFlat.pi_of_span_eq_top` — a finite product of `Away (f i)`
  localizations along a covering family (`span (range f) = ⊤`) is faithfully flat.
* `Algebra.TensorProduct.piRightAlgEquiv`, `piLeftAlgEquiv`, `piPiAlgEquiv` — tensor
  products distribute over finite products of algebras, as `A`-algebra equivalences, with
  pure-tensor `simp` formulas.
* `IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfDvd` — the canonical map `A[1/f] →ₐ[A] A[1/g]` for `f ∣ g`
  (any two such maps are equal: `IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton`).
* `IsLocalization.Away.tensor`, `IsLocalization.Away.tensorEquiv` — the tensor product of
  `Away f` and `Away g` localizations is an `Away (f * g)` localization, hence canonically
  isomorphic to any other model of it.

Everything is elementary commutative algebra; the file is deliberately scheme-free and
shaped for mathlib.
-/

universe u

open TensorProduct

section PiExt

variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
variable {S : ι → Type u} [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra A (S i)]
variable {C : Type u} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]

/-- **The pi-ext lemma.**  Two `A`-algebra maps out of a finite product of localizations

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.InvertibleModule
7	
8	/-!
9	# Descent data from unit 1-cocycles, and the Picard class of a cocycle
10	
11	Let `A → B` be a map of commutative rings.  A **descent 1-cocycle** is a unit
12	`u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` that is normalized along the multiplication `B ⊗[A] B → B` and satisfies
13	the 1-cocycle identity in `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] B` (`Module.IsDescentCocycle`).  Such a unit
14	twists the trivial descent datum on the `B`-module `B`: the coaction `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`
15	is a descent datum in the comodule form of `AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent`
16	(`Module.DescentDatum.ofUnit`), so for faithfully flat `A → B` it descends to an invertible
17	`A`-module `hu.descended` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.InvertibleModule`), whose class in
18	mathlib's Picard group is `hu.picClass : CommRing.Pic A`.
19	
20	This file develops the full calculus of `picClass`, which is the algebraic heart of the
21	dictionary between the Čech Picard group of an affine scheme and `CommRing.Pic`
22	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine`):
23	
24	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_one`: the trivial cocycle has trivial class.
25	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_mul`: `picClass` is multiplicative in the cocycle.
26	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_descentCoboundary_mul`: `picClass` is invariant under
27	  multiplication by the coboundary `β ↦ (1 ⊗ β) * (β ⊗ 1)⁻¹` of a unit `β : Bˣ`.
28	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_map`: `picClass` is invariant under base change of the
29	  cocycle along a map `h : B →ₐ[A] B'` of faithfully flat `A`-algebras.
30	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_eq_one_iff`: the class is trivial **iff** the cocycle
31	  is a coboundary.
32	
33	Everything is pinned to a single universe `u`, matching
34	`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent`.
35	-/
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open TensorProduct
40	
41	namespace Module
42	
43	variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
44	
45	/-! ## The simplicial ring maps in low degrees -/
46	
47	/-- The first-factor inclusion `B → B ⊗[A] B`, `b ↦ b ⊗ₜ 1`. -/
48	abbrev descentIncl₁ : B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] B := Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
49	
50	/-- The second-factor inclusion `B → B ⊗[A] B`, `b ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ b`. -/
51	abbrev descentIncl₂ : B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] B := Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
52	
53	/-- The face map `B ⊗[A] B → B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` hitting tensor positions `1, 2`:
54	`x ⊗ₜ y ↦ x ⊗ₜ (y ⊗ₜ 1)`. -/
55	noncomputable abbrev descentFace₁₂ : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
56	  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A B) Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
57	
58	/-- The face map `B ⊗[A] B → B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` hitting tensor positions `1, 3`:
59	`x ⊗ₜ y ↦ x ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ y)`. -/
60	noncomputable abbrev descentFace₁₃ : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
61	  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A B) Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
62	
63	/-- The face map `B ⊗[A] B → B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` hitting tensor positions `2, 3`:
64	`w ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ w`. -/
65	abbrev descentFace₂₃ : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
67	
68	variable {A B}
69	
70	@[simp]
71	lemma descentIncl₁_apply (b : B) : descentIncl₁ A B b = b ⊗ₜ 1 := rfl
72	
73	@[simp]
74	lemma descentIncl₂_apply (b : B) : descentIncl₂ A B b = 1 ⊗ₜ b := rfl
75	
76	@[simp]
77	lemma descentFace₁₂_tmul (x y : B) : descentFace₁₂ A B (x ⊗ₜ y) = x ⊗ₜ (y ⊗ₜ 1) := rfl
78	
79	@[simp]
80	lemma descentFace₁₃_tmul (x y : B) : descentFace₁₃ A B (x ⊗ₜ y) = x ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ y) := rfl
81	
82	@[simp]
83	lemma descentFace₂₃_apply (w : B ⊗[A] B) : descentFace₂₃ A B w = 1 ⊗ₜ w := rfl
84	
85	/-! ## Descent 1-cocycles -/
86	
87	/-- A **descent 1-cocycle** relative to `A → B`: a unit of `B ⊗[A] B`, normalized along
88	the multiplication map, satisfying the 1-cocycle identity in `B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)`.  For
89	`B = ∏ i, A_{fᵢ}` a finite product of localizations covering `Spec A`, this is exactly a
90	Čech 1-cocycle of units on the cover by the basic opens `D(fᵢ)`. -/
91	structure IsDescentCocycle (u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ) : Prop where
92	  /-- Normalization: the multiplication `B ⊗[A] B → B` sends the cocycle to `1`. -/
93	  lmul'_eq_one : Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) u.val = 1
94	  /-- The 1-cocycle identity. -/
95	  cocycle : descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B u.val = descentFace₁₃ A B u.val
96	
97	/-- The trivial unit is a descent cocycle. -/
98	theorem IsDescentCocycle.one : IsDescentCocycle (1 : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ) where
99	  lmul'_eq_one := by simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]
100	  cocycle := by simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]
101	
102	/-- Descent cocycles are closed under multiplication. -/
103	theorem IsDescentCocycle.mul {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
104	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) : IsDescentCocycle (u * v) where
105	  lmul'_eq_one := by
106	    rw [Units.val_mul, map_mul, hu.lmul'_eq_one, hv.lmul'_eq_one, one_mul]
107	  cocycle := by
108	    simp only [Units.val_mul, map_mul]
109	    rw [show descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₂₃ A B v.val *
110	          (descentFace₁₂ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B v.val)
111	        = descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B u.val *
112	          (descentFace₂₃ A B v.val * descentFace₁₂ A B v.val) by ring]
113	    rw [hu.cocycle, hv.cocycle]
114	
115	/-! ## The descent datum of a cocycle -/
116	
117	variable (u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ)
118	
119	variable (A B) in
120	/-- The coaction `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)` associated with a unit of `B ⊗[A] B`, as a `B`-linear
121	map (with `B` acting on the left tensor factor of the target). -/
122	noncomputable def unitCoaction : B →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] B where
123	  toFun x := u.val * x ⊗ₜ 1
124	  map_add' x y := by rw [add_tmul, mul_add]
125	  map_smul' b x := by
126	    rw [RingHom.id_apply, ← smul_tmul', mul_smul_comm]
127	
128	@[simp]
129	lemma unitCoaction_apply (x : B) : unitCoaction A B u x = u.val * x ⊗ₜ 1 := rfl
130	
131	/-- The action map `B ⊗[A] B →ₗ[B] B` of `ModuleDescent` is the multiplication map. -/
132	lemma actionMap_eq_lmul' (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
133	    actionMap A B B w = Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) w := by
134	  induction w with
135	  | zero => simp
136	  | tmul b m => simp [smul_eq_mul]
137	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
138	
139	/-- The base change to `B` of the coaction is left multiplication by `1 ⊗ₜ u` composed
140	with the face map `descentFace₁₂`. -/
141	lemma baseChange_unitCoaction (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
142	    ((unitCoaction A B u).restrictScalars A).baseChange B w
143	      = descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B w := by
144	  induction w with
145	  | zero => simp
146	  | tmul y z => sorry
147	    -- LHS = `y ⊗ₜ (u * (z ⊗ₜ 1))`; RHS = `(1 ⊗ₜ u) * (y ⊗ₜ (z ⊗ₜ 1))`, equal by
148	    -- `Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul` and `one_mul`.
149	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy, mul_add]
150	
151	/-- The base change to `B` of `x ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ x` is the face map `descentFace₁₃`. -/
152	lemma baseChange_mk_one (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
153	    (TensorProduct.mk A B B 1).baseChange B w = descentFace₁₃ A B w := by
154	  induction w with
155	  | zero => simp
156	  | tmul y z => rfl
157	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
158	
159	/-- The descent datum on the `B`-module `B` associated with a descent 1-cocycle: the
160	coaction is `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`; counitality is the normalization and coassociativity is
161	the cocycle identity. -/
162	noncomputable def DescentDatum.ofUnit (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : DescentDatum A B B where
163	  coaction := unitCoaction A B u
164	  counit m := by
165	    rw [unitCoaction_apply, actionMap_eq_lmul', map_mul, hu.lmul'_eq_one, one_mul,
166	      Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'_apply_tmul, mul_one]
167	  coassoc m := by
168	    -- after rewriting, both sides are `descentFace₁₃ u * (m ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ 1))`
169	    rw [unitCoaction_apply, baseChange_unitCoaction, baseChange_mk_one, map_mul,
170	      ← mul_assoc, hu.cocycle, map_mul]
171	
172	/-- The descended `A`-module of a descent 1-cocycle: the submodule of `x : B` with
173	`u * (x ⊗ₜ 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ x`. -/
174	noncomputable def IsDescentCocycle.descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
175	    Submodule A B :=
176	  (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descended
177	
178	lemma IsDescentCocycle.mem_descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) {m : B} :
179	    m ∈ hu.descended ↔ u.val * m ⊗ₜ 1 = 1 ⊗ₜ m :=
180	  DescentDatum.mem_descended _
181	
182	/-! ## The Picard class of a cocycle -/
183	
184	section picClass
185	
186	variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
187	
188	/-- The descended module of a descent cocycle along a faithfully flat `A → B` is an
189	invertible `A`-module. -/
190	instance IsDescentCocycle.invertible_descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
191	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : Module.Invertible A hu.descended :=
192	  (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).invertible_descended
193	
194	/-- The class in the Picard group of `A` of the module descended from a descent
195	1-cocycle relative to a faithfully flat `A → B`. -/
196	noncomputable def IsDescentCocycle.picClass {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
197	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : CommRing.Pic A :=
198	  CommRing.Pic.mk A hu.descended
199	
200	/-- The descended module of the trivial cocycle is `A` itself (Amitsur exactness in
201	degree `0`). -/
202	noncomputable def descendedOneEquiv :
203	    (IsDescentCocycle.one (A := A) (B := B)).descended ≃ₗ[A] A := by
204	  -- Route: `(DescentDatum.ofUnit 1 .one).equivDescended e he |>.symm` with
205	  -- `e : B ⊗[A] A ≃ₗ[B] B := AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B`; the compatibility `he` is the
206	  -- computation `(a • b) ⊗ₜ 1 = b ⊗ₜ (a • 1)` (`tmul_smul` and `smul_tmul'`) on pure
207	  -- tensors, extended by linearity via `TensorProduct.induction_on`.
208	  sorry
209	
210	@[simp]
211	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_one :
212	    (IsDescentCocycle.one (A := A) (B := B)).picClass = 1 :=
213	  CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff.mpr ⟨descendedOneEquiv⟩
214	
215	/-- The descended module is multiplicative in the cocycle: `descended (u * v)` is the
216	tensor product of `descended u` and `descended v`. -/
217	noncomputable def descendedMulEquiv {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
218	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) :
219	    (hu.descended ⊗[A] hv.descended) ≃ₗ[A] (hu.mul hv).descended := by
220	  -- Route: `equivDescended (DescentDatum.ofUnit (u*v) (hu.mul hv)) e he` where
221	  -- `e : B ⊗[A] (M ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] B` is the composite
222	  -- `AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange` ≪≫ congr (descentEquiv hu) (descentEquiv hv)
223	  --   ≪≫ (B ⊗[B] B ≃ B)`,
224	  -- which on pure tensors is `b ⊗ₜ (m ⊗ₜ n) ↦ b * m * n`.  The compatibility `he` reduces
225	  -- on pure tensors to the ring computation
226	  -- `(u*v) * (b*m*n ⊗ₜ 1) = (b ⊗ₜ 1) * (u * (m ⊗ₜ 1)) * (v * (n ⊗ₜ 1))
227	  --   = (b ⊗ₜ 1) * (1 ⊗ₜ m) * (1 ⊗ₜ n) = b ⊗ₜ (m*n)`
228	  -- using `hu.mem_descended`/`hv.mem_descended` for the members `m, n`.
229	  sorry
230	
231	@[simp]
232	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_mul {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
233	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) :
234	    (hu.mul hv).picClass = hu.picClass * hv.picClass := by
235	  rw [picClass, picClass, picClass, ← CommRing.Pic.mk_tensor]
236	  exact CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(descendedMulEquiv hu hv).symm⟩
237	
238	end picClass
239	
240	/-! ## Coboundaries -/
241	
242	variable (A B) in
243	/-- The descent coboundary of a unit `β : Bˣ`: the unit `(1 ⊗ₜ β) * (β ⊗ₜ 1)⁻¹` of
244	`B ⊗[A] B`. -/
245	noncomputable def descentCoboundary (β : Bˣ) : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ :=
246	  Units.map (descentIncl₂ A B).toRingHom.toMonoidHom β
247	    * (Units.map (descentIncl₁ A B).toRingHom.toMonoidHom β)⁻¹

249	lemma descentCoboundary_val (β : Bˣ) :
250	    (descentCoboundary A B β).val = (1 ⊗ₜ β.val) * ((β⁻¹).val ⊗ₜ 1) := rfl

252	/-- Coboundaries are descent cocycles. -/
253	theorem isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary (β : Bˣ) :
254	    IsDescentCocycle (descentCoboundary A B β) where
255	  lmul'_eq_one := by
256	    -- `lmul' ((1 ⊗ β)(β⁻¹ ⊗ 1)) = β * β⁻¹ = 1`.
257	    sorry
258	  cocycle := by
259	    -- Writing `j₁ β = β ⊗ 1 ⊗ 1`, `j₂ β = 1 ⊗ β ⊗ 1`, `j₃ β = 1 ⊗ 1 ⊗ β`, the three
260	    -- faces of the coboundary are `descentFace₂₃ c = j₃β * (j₂β)⁻¹`,
261	    -- `descentFace₁₂ c = j₂β * (j₁β)⁻¹`, `descentFace₁₃ c = j₃β * (j₁β)⁻¹`, and the
262	    -- cocycle identity is the telescoping product.
263	    sorry

265	/-- Multiplying a cocycle by a coboundary does not change the descended module: the
266	twist is `m ↦ β * m`. -/
267	noncomputable def descendedCoboundaryMulEquiv (β : Bˣ) {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
268	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
269	    hu.descended ≃ₗ[A] ((isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary β).mul hu).descended := by
270	  -- `m ∈ descended u` iff `u * (m ⊗ₜ 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ m`; then
271	  -- `(c * u) * ((β*m) ⊗ₜ 1) = (1 ⊗ₜ β) * (β⁻¹ ⊗ₜ 1) * (β ⊗ₜ 1) * (u * (m ⊗ₜ 1))
272	  --   = (1 ⊗ₜ β) * (1 ⊗ₜ m) = 1 ⊗ₜ (β*m)`,
273	  -- so multiplication by `β` (with inverse `β⁻¹`) is a bijection between the two
274	  -- submodules, `A`-linear since `β • ·` commutes with the `A`-action.
275	  sorry

281	@[simp]
282	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_descentCoboundary_mul (β : Bˣ) {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
283	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
284	    ((isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary β).mul hu).picClass = hu.picClass :=
285	  (CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(descendedCoboundaryMulEquiv β hu).symm⟩)

287	/-- A descent cocycle whose descended module is free is a coboundary; the coboundary unit
288	is the image in `B` of a generator. -/
289	theorem IsDescentCocycle.eq_descentCoboundary_of_equiv {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
290	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) (e : hu.descended ≃ₗ[A] A) :
291	    ∃ β : Bˣ, u = descentCoboundary A B β := by
292	  -- Let `m₀ := (e.symm 1 : B)`.  The composite
293	  -- `B ≃ B ⊗[A] A ≃ B ⊗[A] descended u ≃ B`  (rid⁻¹, base change of `e.symm`,

295	  -- surjectivity at `1` provides `c` with `m₀ * c = 1` and `m₀` is a unit `β`.
296	  -- Membership `m₀ ∈ descended u` says `u * (m₀ ⊗ₜ 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ m₀`, i.e.
297	  -- `u * (descentIncl₁ β) = descentIncl₂ β`, i.e. `u = descentCoboundary β` by `Units.ext`.

302	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) (huv : u = v) : hu.picClass = hv.picClass := by
303	  subst huv; rfl

306	cocycle is a coboundary. -/
307	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_eq_one_iff {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :

309	  constructor
310	  · intro h1
311	    exact hu.eq_descentCoboundary_of_equiv (CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff.mp h1).some
312	  · rintro ⟨β, rfl⟩

315	    rw [IsDescentCocycle.picClass_one] at h
316	    exact (IsDescentCocycle.picClass_congr _ _ (mul_one _).symm).trans h

339	    {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :

9	/-!
10	# Faithfully flat descent of modules
11	
12	Let `A → B` be a map of commutative rings and let `M` be a `B`-module.  This file defines
13	descent data on `M` relative to `A → B`, constructs the descended `A`-module `M₀` as an
14	equalizer submodule of `M`, and proves the two fundamental theorems of flat descent for
15	modules:
16	
17	* **effectivity**: if `B` is flat over `A`, the canonical comparison map
18	  `B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` is an isomorphism;
19	* **uniqueness**: if `B` is faithfully flat over `A`, then any `A`-module `N` equipped with
20	  a `B`-module isomorphism `B ⊗[A] N ≃ M` matching the descent datum is canonically
21	  isomorphic to `M₀`.  The engine is the degree `≤ 1` exactness of the Amitsur complex
22	  `0 → N → B ⊗[A] N ⇉ B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] N`.
23	
24	## Design notes
25	
26	* **Comodule form of a descent datum.**  Classically a descent datum on `M` is a
27	  `B ⊗[A] B`-module isomorphism `φ : M ⊗[A] B ≃ B ⊗[A] M` satisfying a cocycle condition
28	  over the triple tensor product.  We use the equivalent *comodule* (Sweedler-coring)
29	  presentation: a `B`-linear coaction `δ : M →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] M` (with `B` acting on the left
30	  tensor factor of the target) such that
31	  - (`counit`) the action map `B ⊗[A] M → M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`, retracts `δ`, and
32	  - (`coassoc`) the two natural liftings of `δ` to `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] M` agree on the image
33	    of `δ`.
34	
35	  The dictionary: given `φ`, set `δ m := φ (m ⊗ₜ 1)`; then `B ⊗ B`-linearity of `φ` makes
36	  `δ` `B`-linear and recovers `φ` via `φ (m ⊗ₜ b) = (1 ⊗ b) • δ m`, the cocycle condition
37	  becomes `coassoc`, and the standard normalization becomes `counit`.  Conversely the `φ`
38	  associated to a coaction is automatically invertible.  This presentation avoids putting
39	  (several!) `B ⊗[A] B`-module structures on `B ⊗[A] M` and `M ⊗[A] B`, which do not exist
40	  as mathlib instances.  For a unit `u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` whose associated `φ` is
41	  `u • ·` on `M = B`, the coaction is `δ x = u.val * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`.
42	
43	* **The descended module** is the equalizer `M₀ = {m : M | δ m = 1 ⊗ₜ m}`, an `A`-submodule
44	  of `M`, realized as the kernel of the `A`-linear map `δ - (1 ⊗ₜ ·)`.
45	
46	* **Effectivity requires only flatness.**  The comparison `B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` is an isomorphism
47	  whenever `B` is flat over `A`: the counit and coassociativity laws make the augmented
48	  complex `M₀ → M ⇉ B ⊗[A] M` contractible after applying `B ⊗[A] -` (the contraction being
49	  the action maps), and flatness identifies `B ⊗[A] M₀` with the corresponding kernel.
50	  Faithful flatness enters only for uniqueness (the Amitsur exactness `N ≅ (B ⊗[A] N)₀`).
51	
52	* Everything is pinned to a single universe `u`; multi-universe binders interact badly with
53	  the tensor-product instance search in downstream files.
54	
55	## Main declarations
56	
57	* `Module.actionMap A B M : B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M`: the action map `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.
58	* `Module.DescentDatum A B M`: descent data on the `B`-module `M` relative to `A → B`,
59	  in comodule form.
60	* `Module.DescentDatum.baseChange A B N`: the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N`.
61	* `Module.DescentDatum.descended`: the descended `A`-submodule `M₀`.
62	* `Module.DescentDatum.comparison`: the canonical map `B ⊗[A] M₀ →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.
63	* `Module.DescentDatum.comparison_bijective`: **effectivity** — `comparison` is bijective
64	  when `B` is a flat `A`-module.
65	* `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv : B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ₗ[B] M`: the comparison isomorphism.
66	* `Module.DescentDatum.exact_mk_coactionSub`: degree `≤ 1` **Amitsur exactness** for a
67	  faithfully flat `A → B`.
68	* `Module.DescentDatum.unitEquiv : N ≃ₗ[A] (baseChange A B N).descended`: the unit of
69	  descent is an isomorphism (faithfully flat case).
70	* `Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended`: **uniqueness** — an `A`-module `N` with a
71	  datum-compatible isomorphism `B ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[B] M` is canonically `A`-isomorphic to `M₀`.
72	  Two descents of the same datum are therefore canonically isomorphic.
73	-/

81	variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
82	variable (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
83	
84	/-- The `B`-linear action map `B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`, of a `B`-module `M`. -/
85	noncomputable def actionMap : B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M :=
86	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (LinearMap.id (R := A) (M := M))
87	
88	@[simp] theorem actionMap_tmul (b : B) (m : M) : actionMap A B M (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • m := rfl
89	
90	theorem actionMap_one_tmul (m : M) : actionMap A B M (1 ⊗ₜ m) = m := by simp
91	
92	variable {A B M}
93	
94	section actionMap
95	
96	variable {X Y : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
97	
98	/-- Naturality of the action map in `B`-linear maps. -/
99	theorem actionMap_baseChange [Module B X] [IsScalarTower A B X]
100	    [AddCommGroup Y] [Module A Y] [Module B Y] [IsScalarTower A B Y]
101	    (g : X →ₗ[B] Y) (x : B ⊗[A] X) :
102	    actionMap A B Y ((g.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x) = g (actionMap A B X x) := by
103	  induction x with
104	  | zero => simp
105	  | tmul b m => simp
106	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
107	
108	/-- The action map of `B ⊗[A] X` retracts the base change of `x ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ x`. -/
109	theorem actionMap_baseChange_mk (x : B ⊗[A] X) :
110	    actionMap A B (B ⊗[A] X) ((TensorProduct.mk A B X 1).baseChange B x) = x := by
111	  induction x with
112	  | zero => simp
113	  | tmul b m => simp [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
114	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
115	
116	end actionMap

118	variable (A B M) in
119	/-- A descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to `A → B`, in comodule (Sweedler-coring)
120	form: a `B`-linear coaction `δ : M → B ⊗[A] M` (`B` acting through the left tensor factor
121	of the target) that is counital and coassociative.  This is equivalent to the classical
122	formulation via a `B ⊗[A] B`-linear cocycle isomorphism `M ⊗[A] B ≃ B ⊗[A] M`; see the
123	module docstring for the dictionary. -/
124	structure DescentDatum where
125	  /-- The coaction of the descent datum. -/
126	  coaction : M →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] M
127	  /-- The action map retracts the coaction. -/
128	  counit (m : M) : actionMap A B M (coaction m) = m
129	  /-- Coassociativity: the two liftings of the coaction to `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] M` agree on
130	  coaction values.  In the classical dictionary this is the cocycle condition. -/
131	  coassoc (m : M) :
132	    (coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B (coaction m) =
133	      (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B (coaction m)
134	
135	namespace DescentDatum
136	
137	variable (A B) in
138	/-- The canonical descent datum on a base change `B ⊗[A] N`, with coaction
139	`b ⊗ₜ n ↦ b ⊗ₜ 1 ⊗ₜ n`. -/
140	@[simps coaction]
141	noncomputable def baseChange (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
142	    DescentDatum A B (B ⊗[A] N) where
143	  coaction := (TensorProduct.mk A B N 1).baseChange B
144	  counit x := by
145	    induction x with
146	    | zero => simp
147	    | tmul b n => simp [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
148	    | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
149	  coassoc x := by
150	    induction x with
151	    | zero => simp
152	    | tmul b n => simp
153	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
154	
155	variable (D : DescentDatum A B M)
156	
157	/-- The `A`-linear difference between the coaction and the canonical map `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`;
158	its kernel is the descended module. -/
159	def coactionSub : M →ₗ[A] B ⊗[A] M :=
160	  D.coaction.restrictScalars A - TensorProduct.mk A B M 1
161	
162	@[simp] theorem coactionSub_apply (m : M) : D.coactionSub m = D.coaction m - 1 ⊗ₜ m := rfl
163	
164	/-- The descended `A`-module of a descent datum: the equalizer
165	`M₀ = {m : M | δ m = 1 ⊗ₜ m}`. -/
166	def descended : Submodule A M := LinearMap.ker D.coactionSub
167	
168	theorem mem_descended {m : M} : m ∈ D.descended ↔ D.coaction m = 1 ⊗ₜ m := by
169	  rw [descended, LinearMap.mem_ker, coactionSub_apply, sub_eq_zero]
170	
171	/-- The canonical comparison map `B ⊗[A] M₀ →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.  Flat descent
172	(`comparison_bijective`) asserts this is an isomorphism when `B` is flat over `A`. -/
173	noncomputable def comparison : B ⊗[A] D.descended →ₗ[B] M :=
174	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B D.descended.subtype
175	
176	@[simp] theorem comparison_tmul (b : B) (m : D.descended) :
177	    D.comparison (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • (m : M) := rfl
178	
179	theorem comparison_eq_actionMap (x : B ⊗[A] D.descended) :
180	    D.comparison x = actionMap A B M (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B x) := by
181	  induction x with
182	  | zero => simp
183	  | tmul b m => simp
184	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
185	
186	private theorem coactionSub_lTensor_apply (x : B ⊗[A] M) :
187	    D.coactionSub.lTensor B x =
188	      (D.coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x -
189	        (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B x := by
190	  induction x with
191	  | zero => simp
192	  | tmul b m => simp [TensorProduct.tmul_sub]
193	  | add x y hx hy =>
194	      simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
195	      abel
196	
197	/-- The coaction retracts onto the kernel of `coactionSub ⊗ B`: any `x : B ⊗[A] M` on which
198	the two liftings agree is a coaction value, namely of `actionMap x`.  This is the
199	contracting-homotopy computation at the heart of both effectivity and Amitsur exactness. -/
200	theorem coaction_actionMap {x : B ⊗[A] M}
201	    (hx : (D.coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x =
202	      (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B x) :
203	    D.coaction (actionMap A B M x) = x :=
204	  (actionMap_baseChange D.coaction x).symm.trans <| by rw [hx, actionMap_baseChange_mk]
205	
206	/-- **Effectivity of flat descent for modules**: for `B` flat over `A`, the canonical map
207	`B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` out of the descended module is bijective. -/
208	theorem comparison_bijective [Module.Flat A B] : Function.Bijective D.comparison := by
209	  have hexact : Function.Exact (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B) (D.coactionSub.lTensor B) :=
210	    Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B D.coactionSub.exact_subtype_ker_map
211	  have hinj : Function.Injective (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B) :=
212	    Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ D.descended.injective_subtype
213	  have key : ∀ y : B ⊗[A] D.descended,
214	      D.coaction (D.comparison y) = D.descended.subtype.lTensor B y := by
215	    intro y
216	    rw [comparison_eq_actionMap]
217	    refine D.coaction_actionMap (sub_eq_zero.mp ?_)
218	    rw [← coactionSub_lTensor_apply]
219	    exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
220	  constructor
221	  · intro y z hyz
222	    exact hinj (by rw [← key, ← key, hyz])
223	  · intro m
224	    have hm : D.coactionSub.lTensor B (D.coaction m) = 0 := by
225	      rw [coactionSub_lTensor_apply, D.coassoc m, sub_self]
226	    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact _).mp hm
227	    refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
228	    have hcoact : D.coaction (D.comparison y) = D.coaction m := by rw [key y, hy]
229	    have := congrArg (actionMap A B M) hcoact
230	    rwa [D.counit, D.counit] at this
231	
232	/-- The comparison isomorphism `B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ₗ[B] M` of flat descent. -/
233	noncomputable def descentEquiv [Module.Flat A B] : B ⊗[A] D.descended ≃ₗ[B] M :=
234	  LinearEquiv.ofBijective D.comparison D.comparison_bijective
235	
236	@[simp] theorem descentEquiv_tmul [Module.Flat A B] (b : B) (m : D.descended) :
237	    D.descentEquiv (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • (m : M) := rfl

239	section Amitsur
